News.title: Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double
News.content:
Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

News.title: Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start
News.content:
Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he said.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

News.title: Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off
News.content:
Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

News.title: Bird flu threatens French foie gras amid new duck cull
News.content:
The latest cull - like previous ones - was undertaken to protect both animal and human health.

Ducks are killed to stop the spread of the disease between farms, as well as to protect the health of farmers and minimise the risk of the virus mutating.

It is thought foie gras itself does not pose a risk to human health, even if it came from a bird-flu-infected duck, because it is almost always heat-treated before it is sold, which effectively destroys the virus, according to Public Health France.

“The consumption of meat, foie gras and eggs – and more generally of any food product based on poultry – presents no risk to humans,” said a spokesman for the Maine-et-Loire prefecture.

Veterinary experts say ducks are especially problematic regarding H5N1 because they can carry the virus without showing symptoms and have been described as the Chevaux de Troie or “Trojan horses” of bird flu.

It is unclear how the birds in the latest outbreak, located on a farm in Longué-Jumelles, contracted the virus, although it is typically spread by wild birds which shed the virus through their droppings.

It is for this reason that British poultry were forced into lockdown or “flockdown” from late October to April of this year.

This included so-called “free-range” birds, which, as the Telegraph reported in November continued to be described as free-range despite never seeing the light of day under a dispensation given by the Department for Environment, Food, and Rural Affairs (DEFRA).

Ducks reared for foie gras typically spend the first 90 days of their lives being reared in their tens of thousands in barns with very little access to natural light.

Animal rights campaigners say most never see water.

They then are put through a rigorous 12-16 day “fattening up” period where they are force-fed through a tube to significantly enlarge their livers, before being slaughtered.

While France introduced a vaccination programme to protect its duck population from bird flu in 2023, the jabs do not entirely stop the virus from getting into a flock.

Data collected by the French Agency for Food, Environmental and Occupational Health & Safety suggested that between 50 and 55 per cent of the country’s ducks are unvaccinated at any given time, due to a 20-day gap between the first and second dose of the vaccine and waning immunity over time.

The ducks subject to the latest bird-flu cull in Western France had received their first dose of the H5N1 vaccine, but not the second, meaning they were not fully protected, according to the disease monitoring firm Airfinity.

The threat to France’s £2 billion foie gras industry comes amid increasing global competition.

Once the dominant producer, it is now being challenged by China, which has rapidly scaled up its output of the delicacy and now accounts for 45 per cent of global production.

A tin of Chinese foie gras costs roughly £3.70, while a typical tin of French foie gras made from duck liver costs between £10 and £15. French foie gras produced from Geese costs anywhere between £70 and £150.

China is also said to operate a more rigorous poultry vaccination programme, according to an analysis by DEFRA.

It applies to all farmed birds in the country, which has managed to keep outbreaks of bird flu on farms relatively low compared with European levels.

The H5N1 avian flu pandemic has now been running for six years and has decimated flocks of farmed chickens and turkeys across the globe.

In the UK alone, more than five million farmed birds have been culled since 2021, costing an estimated £48 million in farmers’ compensation alone.

Last week, the virus was detected on a mink farm in the US state of Utah.

Minks in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of fur farms – where thousands of the animals are crammed together in tight proximity – give invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate.

The virus has also done huge damage to wild birds and other animals. In South America alone, more than 600,000 wild seabirds have died since 2022.

Dozens of other mammals have been infected and died across the globe, including foxes, otters, sea lions, bears, and seals.

In June, the virus was found in Australia for the first time – the last continent on earth to record a case – and the government has since launched a vaccination programme to protect the country’s rare species, including birds like orange-bellied parrots and black cockatoos.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 gains the mutations necessary to spread between people, it could trigger a human-pandemic, something that would be of “enormous concern”, according to the World Health Organization (WHO), given the virus’s 50 per cent case fatality rate.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: The Chancellor’s speech, as it happened
News.content:
John Healey failed to rule out tax rises at next month’s Budget in his first major speech as Chancellor.

Mr Healey also sought to blame Liz Truss and her mini-Budget in 2022 for the high borrowing costs being paid by the Treasury.

During a speech in Coventry, the Chancellor said he would be “honest” about the need to control public spending during his time in Number 11.

He was speaking days after the cost of government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007.

It was also overshadowed by Jaguar Land Rover announcing plans to cut 4,000 jobs in the face of “intense competition and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty”.

Read our report on the Chancellor’s speech.

News.title: Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

Sports.title: Julian Alvarez 'suffering' after failed Arsenal transfer as statement made before Liverpool
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez 'suffering' after failed Arsenal transfer as statement made before Liverpool

Julian Alvarez is in contention to feature for Atletico Madrid in their Champions League clash against Liverpool on Wednesday, with the Argentine yet to start a game this season

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez is expected to feature for Atletico Madrid against Liverpool (Image: Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

Atletico Madrid president Enrique Cerezo has claimed that Julian Alvarez is "suffering" amid a summer of transfer speculation that saw him linked with a move to Barcelona and Arsenal.

‌



Alvarez is yet to start a match for Atletico this season after he came close to leaving the club. The Argentine was understood to be pushing for a move to Barca and made no secret of his desire to quit Atletico.

‌



Arsenal, meanwhile, had placed Alvarez high up on their shortlist as Mikel Arteta tried to strengthen his front line, with sporting director Andrea Berta trying to convince the ex-Manchester City man to move back to the Premier League, having worked with him at Atletico.

‌



Despite Barca offering more than £86million and fierce backlash from the Atletico supporters, Diego Simeone's side ended up keeping hold of Alvarez beyond the transfer deadline. With that, Alvarez is in contention to feature for Atletico ahead of their Champions League opener against Liverpool on Wednesday after being named in the travelling squad.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Speaking hours before the game at Anfield, Cerezo provided an update on Alvarez's current condition and believes he is still coming to terms of failing to secure a move away from Atletico.

In an interview with Spanish newspaper Sport, Cerezo said: "I see Alvarez in good shape, but the truth is that he is suffering after what happened recently, and that is a cause for concern."

He added: "I think his recovery is going well, and when the coach sees that the time is right, he will return to play. The Julian case is closed."

‌



Alvarez, who came off the bench in Saturday's 3-0 defeat at Athletic Club, has been named in Atletico's travelling squad for the Liverpool fixture and is anticipated to feature as a substitute, after Diego Simeone admitted he doesn't see the ex-Manchester City man "starting yet".

When asked about Alvarez in his pre-Liverpool press conference, Simeone said: "Julian is still developing; I don't see him starting yet, but he'll help us as the game progresses."

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez is now back in the fold at Atletico Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Regarding Atletico's other striking options, both Jonathan David and Alexander Sorloth are doubts, suggesting Lee Kang-in and Alex Baena could once again be deployed up front.

"Jonathan arrived very recently and couldn't play the other day [against Athletic Club] due to a problem," Simeone said. "[Sorloth's] recovering. He has this injury that's keeping him from playing. We need him; he's important, whether it's for 90, 60 or 20 minutes. He gives us things we don't have in the team right now. Hopefully, he'll be back soon."

Simeone added: "It's very important for the club that the final is at the Metropolitano. For us, we have to work incredibly hard to be able to aspire to that privileged position.

‌



"We're in a growth phase, settling in; there are many new players, the situation with Julian, David's arrival at the end of the transfer window, the national team players who arrived late and nobody cares about them anymore. Little by little, we'll find our rhythm."

Alvarez has managed just 55 minutes of football all season, but looks set to build on that and clock up further game time against Liverpool.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick explains why Luke Shaw missed Man Utd training with transfer failure clear
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick explains why Luke Shaw missed Man Utd training with transfer failure clear

Manchester United host Sabah in their opening Champions League game of the season on Thursday night and Michael Carrick has been forced to address concerns over Luke Shaw

View 2 Images Michael Carrick spoke ahead of Manchester United's first Champions League tie (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United's decision not to sign a left-back in the summer transfer window has been put under scrutiny after Luke Shaw missed a training session ahead of their opening Champions League game of the season.

‌



United went into the transfer window keen to bring in some competition for Shaw, but failed to sign one, with top target Lewis Hall unavailable from Newcastle. Shaw played all 38 Premier League games for United last season, but the club have a tougher challenge this season having returned to the Champions League.

‌



The challenge facing Michael Carrick is clear this week, with the derby against Manchester City coming on Sunday on the back of Thursday's Champions League game against debutants Sabah. With just one senior specialist left-back in the squad, Shaw's fitness and durability will come under the microscope.

‌



The 31-year-old was absent from Wednesday's training session, raising concerns over his availability. But Carrick played down any hint of an injury in his pre-match press conference.

‌



"We just gave him an extra recovery day today," he said. "We'll see by tomorrow how he is, but it's not an ongoing thing or a plan or anything like that. It was just off the back of the game the other day. Each individual has kind of different little things that we manage and Luke was one of them today."

With academy graduate left-back Harry Amass not in the squad, it was Noussair Mazraoui who replaced Shaw off the bench in the 2-2 draw with Everton on the weekend. Mazraoui, Patrick Dorgu and Diogo Dalot are the most likely alternatives to Shaw.

Carrick knows he will have to use his squad to manage the busy fixture schedule. Asked whether rotation would come against the team from Azerbaijan on Thursday night at Old Trafford, Carrick made his approach clear.

‌



View 2 Images Luke Shaw is the only senior specialist left-back at Manchester United (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

"It's a balanced view, that's why we've got the squad," he said. "We need to adapt to certain strengths and different ways of playing. We play Thursday, Wednesday, it's about managing the group and trusting them and anyone who can play will play."

The Manchester Derby comes quickly on the back of Thursday's game, but Carrick refused to complain. "I'm not concerned," he said. "It's not ideal, but it's not something we can do much about. We've got to deal with the cards we were dealt."

‌



The depth in defence has been given a boost by the return to training of Matthias de Ligt, who hasn't played since the end of November, having undergone back surgery in May.

"It's positive. Matta has trained really well," said Carrick. "I think when you're out for such a long period of time and you get right to the final stages and you push and you push, you've got to manage that last stage. It's important.

"We've got to get that balance right for when to take the next step. But he's on a good track, he's in a good place, and it's great to have him back around us, and hopefully it'll be sometime soon."

Sports.title: Man City and Premier League 'braced for £100m bill' as huge claim made about 115 charges case
Sports.content:
Man City and Premier League 'braced for £100m bill' as huge claim made about 115 charges case

The Premier League's legal battle with Manchester City has still not seen a result and has been ongoing for almost two years since the 12-week hearing finished in 2024

View 2 Images The outcome of the Premier League's legal battle with Manchester City is still unknown (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Manchester City and the Premier League's legal battle is estimated to have cost each over £100m and may have already reached the appeal stage, according to football finance expert Kieran Maguire. City were charged with 115 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules in February 2023, but no result has been forthcoming.

‌



Maguire, who admits he has no evidence to support such a suspicion, said he would not be surprised if one party were appealing an initial finding, given the silence around the case. He highlighted a similar situation with Chelsea, where the news did not emerge until after their appeal over 78 charges.

‌



A 12-week hearing into the charges against City concluded in December 2024. With the two-year mark approaching, the independent commission is yet to publish a ruling on the complex case, with City strongly denying the allegations they face.

‌



"We are probably talking hundreds and hundreds of thousands of pieces of evidence, and they have to be gone through with a fine-tooth comb," Maguire said on the Rest is Football podcast.

"We saw with the Chelsea case, where Chelsea had 78 charges, that the verdict was given and Chelsea effectively appealed and that took another 3 or 4 months to work out.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"So we could be in a situation, and I have no evidence to back this up, that there has been a decision made on Manchester City and either the Premier League or Manchester City have immediately appealed and we are now actually working out way through the appeal process to get a final, final answer. We didn't know that (there was an appeal) in terms of Chelsea."

Mirror Sport have approached Manchester City and the Premier League for comment.

In May, it was suggested that a result could still be two years away. The scale of the charges and the severity of the accusations have ensured a long wait for an unprecedented case in English football.

‌



Among City's charges are 54 allegations of failing to provide accurate and up-to-date financial information from 2009 until 2018. They also face 14 alleged breaches of failing to provide accurate financial reports of player and manager compensation over the same period.

View 2 Images Manchester City were handed 115 charges over three years ago. (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"We are now almost two years since the commission first sat, it commenced in September 2024," Maguire said. "It took around about 10-12 weeks to hear all the evidence. As one lawyer said to me, if there are 115 charges, there are 115 defences, so it makes it difficult.

"You have got three people sitting on the commission, all of whom are very high-powered people in their own right, so getting them into the same room at the same time over the course of the last 18-20 months has proven to be very difficult.

"Then, from what I understand and there has been very much a news blackout, you have got to give the people and professionals involved a lot of credit. There are no leaks, no WhatsApp groups with gossip."

‌

The wait is proving costly for both the Premier League and City, however. Maguire believes both will have racked up nine-figure bills.

"These charges are so serious that it is difficult to see how the board of Manchester City could survive if they lose the case and it would be hugely embarrassing for the Premier League if they lose the case because the legal costs for both parties are probably in excess of £100m," Maguire added.

‌



Premier League chief Richard Masters has admitted that the process has taken longer than he hoped. Speaking last month he suggested he was unable to provide an update and that the system must be allowed to take its course.

"Our rules are very clear about that - I have to keep everything confidential until we're ready to hand down a decision and be clear about it," he said. "I can't give any update on timing or what's happening.

"There's only one available route through this, which is to allow the process to take its course. It has taken longer than expected, and I do understand the frustrations."

Article continues below

"I've already said the commission need the time and the space to do their job," he added. "In the end, the Premier League's role is to put allegations, if the evidence is strong enough, in front of an independent commission and allow that commission to establish the truth, and that shouldn't be qualified by the amount of time it takes to get there."

Sports.title: Meet the six people grilling Thomas Tuchel over England's gut-wrenching World Cup exit
Sports.content:
Meet the six people grilling Thomas Tuchel over England's gut-wrenching World Cup exit

Thomas Tuchel is meeting with the FA's performance advisory group where he will be quizzed about England's World Cup efforts

View 5 Images Thomas Tuchel will face questions about England's World Cup performance (Image: Getty)

England boss Thomas Tuchel will stand in front of a six-person panel when he meets with the FA's performance advisory board. The group includes a rugby league legend and a former Premier League player.

‌



The international break will soon be upon us and this hiatus will last an extended three weeks. During this period, the Three Lions will play four Nations League matches, their first outings since July's bitter World Cup semi-final defeat.

‌



England battled their way to the final four in North America, seeing off the likes of Mexico and Norway in the knockout stages, before facing reigning world champions Argentina in Atlanta. Despite going 1-0 up through Anthony Gordon in the 55th minute, late goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez sent Tuchel's passive side packing.

‌



A bronze medal was secured in a bizarre third-place play-off against France, which ended 6-4, meaning the result was England's best at a World Cup since their 1966 victory.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Thomas Tuchel's intensive World Cup inquest as FA prepare major report into England failings READ MORE :

Inside Gareth Southgate's failed management stint from telling letter to beers with players READ MORE :

In preparation for the upcoming break, manager Tuchel was a part of an inquest held at St George's Park at the beginning of the month, where assistant Anthony Barry and his coaching staff joined him for a usual three-day review. FA technical director John McDermott was also present.

‌



But this week, the German will attend a meeting and stand before the FA's performance advisory group as part of a wider probe into the World Cup result. A report will be produced and handed to FA chiefs later this year, so Mirror Football takes a look at the six individuals grilling Tuchel over the Three Lions' performance Stateside.

View 5 Images Tuchel came under fire for how he managed England's semi-final defeat (Image: Getty)

Jobi McAnuff (Chair)

The only former professional footballer in the group, McAnuff was appointed to the FA Board as an independent non-executive director in 2022 and continues to balance this work with punditry duties for the likes of Sky Sports and talkSPORT.

‌



McAnuff enjoyed a stellar career in the Football League, making almost 700 league appearances for the likes of Reading, Leyton Orient, Wimbledon and Watford. He made 38 appearances in the Premier League, all for Reading during the 2012/13 season.

The 44-year-old also earned 32 caps for Jamaica at the senior international level between 2002 and 2016. He retired in 2021, becoming interim manager of Leyton Orient before leaving the club in May of that year. He chairs the group.

View 5 Images McAnuff is an EFL hero (Image: Getty)

‌



Sir Kevin Sinfield

Rugby league icon Kevin Sinfield is one of his sport's most notable faces. The 45-year-old made over 500 appearances for Leeds Rhinos, winning seven Super League titles. He also captained both his club and the England national team.

Away from the pitch, Sinfield has transitioned into coaching. He served as the director of rugby for Leeds Rhinos and also joined Steve Borthwick's coaching staff for England's men's rugby union team.

Following the Motor Neurone Disease (MND) diagnosis of dear friend and former team-mate Rob Burrow, Sinfield completed multiple ultra-marathon challenges, raising over £15million for MND charities and becoming only the second rugby league player in history to be knighted for services to the sport.

‌



View 5 Images Sinfield joins McAnuff in the group (Image: Getty)

Prof Damian Hughes

Professor Damian Hughes is a sports psychologist and organisational consultant. The 54-year-old holds a visiting professorship in Organisational Behaviour and Change at Manchester Metropolitan University.

Hughes has worked directly with various sports teams across football and rugby as a consultant, focusing on building high-performance environments. He co-hosts the aptly-named High Performance Podcast with Jake Humphrey.

‌



Sir Michael Barber

Sir Michael Barber is a former senior civil servant and academic who currently serves as the chancellor of the University of Exeter. He also sits in the House of Lords as Baron Barber of Chittlehampton.

Barber, 70, has advised a handful of governments and international bodies during his career and previously served as chief education advisor at Pearson, a partner at McKinsey & Company, and Chair of the Office for Students.

View 5 Images Barber is also the chairman of Somerset County Cricket Club (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

Col. Lucy Giles

Colonel Lucy Giles is a retired senior officer in the British Army. Her service spanned more than three decades and included deployments to Bosnia, Iraq, Afghanistan, Northern Ireland and Sierra Leone.

She became the first female college commander at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst in 2016, where she trained officer cadets. Giles, who was appointed a CBE in 2024, contributes military-grade leadership models and expertise in high-stress decision-making to the board.

Manoj Badale

British-Indian entrepreneur Manoj Badale is best known within sports as the owner of the Indian Premier League's Rajasthan Royals cricket franchise. The 58-year-old is also an OBE and offers commercial insight to the panel.

Sports.title: Ballon d'Or winner picked as one player blows competition away
Sports.content:
Ballon d'Or winner picked as one player blows competition away

The Ballon d'Or will be decided towards the end of October, but Mirror Football readers have already offered their verdict of who should win

View 2 Images The Ballon d'Or trophy will be awarded on Monday, October 26 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

England captain Harry Kane will win the Ballon d'Or, according to Mirror Football readers. The Bayern Munich forward is among the 30 stars to be nominated for the glamorous award.

‌



Last year, Paris Saint-Germain forward Ousmane Dembele was crowned the victor after he spear-headed Paris Saint-Germain to their first ever Champions League triumph. Kane won the Bundesliga and the DFB Pokal in Germany, and also fired the Three Lions to a third placed finish at the World Cup, scoring six goals in the USA and Mexico.

‌



As well as starring for Thomas Tuchel's side, he also hammered 61 goals and seven assists in 51 appearances in all competitions for the Bavarians. After his phenomenal campaign, Mirror Football's readership believes he will win the Ballon d'Or, after making their thoughts known in the latest poll.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

At the time of writing, 50% of the 1262 respondents voted for Kane to win the Ballon d'Or. On the poll, Kylian Mbappe, who won the World Cup golden boot for the second time, claimed 13% of the votes as the runner-up.

Meanwhile Barcelona superstar and World Cup winner Lamine Yamal was given the bronze with 10% of votes, with Lionel Messi taking 7%. In addition, 20% of voters believe someone else within the nominees deserve the gong.

‌



Kane is not the only England player to make it onto the list.. Real Madrid ace Jude Bellingham has also been nominated for the prize, as has Declan Rice, who won the Premier League and reached the Champions League final with Arsenal.

Former Manchester United midfielder Owen Hargreaves recently tipped the England skipper to become the first Englishman since Michael Owen to win the prize. He said: "I think this year, Harry's the favourite, but there's some other big candidates in there."

‌



He then added: "I think statistics are very important. Bayern had an incredible season, winning the Bundesliga and the German Cup, with Harry scoring the hat-trick in the final.

View 2 Images Harry Kane has enjoyed a brilliant 12 months with Bayern Munich (Image: Getty Images)

"He also got third place at the 2026 World Cup. I think the body of work is there. Harry's ageing like a fine wine. He's only going to get better.

‌



"A lot of people criticised him for making the move to Bayern Munich, but it's actually proven to be the right decision. He's been here for three seasons and two of his best ever seasons, statistically, have been at Bayern Munich."

The Ballon d'Or nominees list in full is as follows: Jude Bellingham, Pau Cubarsi, Marc Cucurella, Ousmane Dembele, Luis Diaz, Bruno Fernandes, Gabriel, Erling Haaland, Achraf Hakimi, Harry Kane, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Lamine Yamal, Sadio Mane, Marquinhos, Lautaro Martinez, Kylian Mbappe, Nuno Mendes, Lionel Messi, Joao Neves, Michael Olise, Willian Pacho, Julian Quinones, Declan Rice, Rodri, Fabian Ruiz, William Saliba, Ferran Torres, Dayot Upamecano, Vinicius Junior, Vitinha.

Sports.title: Arsenal bosses make contact with selling club after early impressions of new signing
Sports.content:
Arsenal bosses make contact with selling club after early impressions of new signing

Arsenal sign Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge in the summer and, after making such an immediate impact, those from the Premier League club were keen to compliment the Belgian side when they crossed paths

View 2 Images Christos Tzolis has made an instant impact after moving to Arsenal

Arsenal officials have been so impressed with Christos Tzolis that they've been telling Club Brugge president Bart Verhaeghe about his exploits.

‌



The Greek winger made a £34million move to the Emirates this summer following two hugely impressive seasons with the Belgian club, where he scored 43 times. Tzolis has gone straight into the Arsenal starting XI and immediately made an impression.

‌



He's helped the Gunners enjoy a perfect start to the season, playing in their Community Shield win, whilst during pre-season his numbers saw him among the best performers.

‌



Arsenal executives came across their Club Brugge counterparts when they headed to the Champions League draw and it was there that they made it known how much of an impact Tzolis has already has.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Verhaeghe told Het Belang van Limburg: "At the Champions League draw, I saw people from Arsenal and they showed a tremendous amount of respect. ‘What a player you’ve delivered’, they told me. They said he has an excellent attitude, is the best in the physical tests and is a great guy, too."

Tzolis has been a fixture for Arsenal in the early part of the season despite the depth of quality they can boast in the final third. Mikel Arteta has picked the Greek star ahead of the likes of Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke whilst Gabriel Martinelli has since left the club.

Tzolis has flourished since his initial spell in English football, which saw him playing for Norwich during their relegation to the Championship. After successive loan spells away he found himself with Club Brugge.

‌



View 2 Images The Greek winger thrived in two seasons at Club Brugge before moving to Arsenal

The Belgian club's president has claimed their recent change in approach is to ensure their players remain attractive to top clubs - and believes they've been vindicated.

He said: "We were the innovators from day one, and we’ll keep innovating.Today, we’re selling players to Arsenal and Inter Milan, two teams that have reached the Champions League final in the last two years."

Article continues below

After seeing Tzolis play for Arsenal for the first time Arteta claimed: “He’s come into the team and really organically he’s fitted in,” Arteta said of Tzolis afterwards. He’s a really intelligent boy, and he has a massive quality, which is that in the last 30 metres, he is so composed to pick people out in and around the box or to finish."

Sports.title: Ballon d'Or power rankings as Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe's chances rated
Sports.content:
It's football's most prestigious and divisive award. And now we're closer to finding out the recipient of the 2026 men's Ballon d'Or.

On Monday, France Football announced the 30 nominees ahead of the ceremony in London on October 26. Stars from the Premier League, Bundesliga, La Liga and beyond were named on the shortlist, kickstarting the debate over who should go home with the gong.

The voting process asks those involved to consider three pieces of criteria. Firslty, individual performances, decisive and impressive character. Secondly, team performances and achievements. And thirdly, class and fair play. Voting should be based on performances between August 3, 2025 and July 19 of this year.

With that in mind, Mirror Football presents its power rankings for the 2026 men's Ballon d'Or.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

30. Julian Quinones

29. Sadio Mane

‌



28. Marc Cucurella

27. Dayot Upamecano

26. Luis Diaz

25. Lautaro Martinez

‌



24. Ferran Torres

23. Willian Pacho

22. Achraf Hakimi

21. Vinicius Junior

‌



20. Bruno Fernandes

It's quite the acheivement to be nominated without having played in a European competition for your club, won a trophy or gone far at an international tournament. But it speaks volumes that Bruno Fernandes has made this list.

Nine goals and a record-breaking 21 assists in the Premier League last season fired Manchester United back into the Champions League, and he's swept up awards ever since, including winning the PFA Player of the Year. Remarkable, although still some way off wining the Ballon d'Or.

19. Marquinhos

Despite playing in nearly twice as many competitions, Marquinhos only made one more appearance that Fernandes at club level last season. That's because PSG prioritised their captain for the Champions League which they successfully defended after beating Arsenal on penalties, adding to another Ligue 1 title win.

‌



But perhaps Marquinhos' finest moment came after the final whistle in Budapest. The 32-year-old went over to console Brazilian compatriot Gabriel Magalhaes after the Arsenal defender missed the decisive penalty. Classy.

18. Jude Bellingham

It was another season to forget for Real Madrid, as they went trophy-less for the second year running and changed managers once again. Jude Bellingham, though, was often there to pull them out of trouble and contributed to 15 goals in all competitions.

But it's his talismanic performances for England at the World Cup that stand out. Driving the Three Lions on during the knockout stages, he made a mockery of anyone questioning his role as a starter under Thomas Tuchel with consistently fabulous displays.

View 7 Images Jude Bellingham and Erling Haaland are both nominated (Image: Hannah Peters - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



17. Joao Neves

While PSG's attackers often garner most the praise, it's their world-class midfield which gives them the platform to be so prolific. Joao Neves is now a two-time Ballon d'Or nominee and deservedly so.

The Portugal international was a genuine contender heading into the World Cup, but his country's underwhelming showing left a lot to be desired. Still, he's integral to the best club side in the world and can't be dismissed.

16. Vitinha

Sticking with PSG and Portugal, Vitinha came third in last year's Ballon d'Or but would do well to break into the top 10 this time around. Of course, the midfielder was a driving force behind his club's success and enjoyed a career-best tally for goals and assists.

There's little to split Vitinha and Neves as players, who have different roles for club and country. But more goal contributions and appearances for the robust former Wolves man gives him the edge.

‌



15. Gabriel Magalhaes

Becoming somewhat of a villain to non-Arsenal fans over the past 12 months, Gabriel has enjoyed another undeniably brilliant 12 months at both ends of the pitch. His imperious displays at the back were complemented by four goals and five assists, showing his prowess from set pieces.

Unfortunately for him, Brazil were drawn against Norway at the World Cup and Gabriel had to come up against Erling Haaland in the last 16. Haaland beat the 28-year-old in the air to break the deadlock late on and that knocked the stuffing out of both Brazil and Gabriel's slim chances of picking up this award.

View 7 Images William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes formed the bedrock of Arsenal's success (Image: Photo by Visionhaus/Getty Images)

14. William Saliba

It's also hard to split the Arsenal centre-backs. They complement each other perfectly and wouldn't be as good without their trusty partner.

‌



They both played the same amount of games, lifted the Premier Leage title and missed out on the World Cup. But Saliba narrowly pips Gabriel in our rankings considering France's deeper run at the tournament and how his injury in their semi-final against Spain was arguably the watershed moment in Les Blues' campaign - and not for the better.

13. Nuno Mendes

Undoubtedly the best player in the world in his position, Nuno Mendes had another year dominating the left flank for PSG. With four goals and one assist in the Champions League, his contribution to their second European triumph was paramount.

But like Saliba, his injury in the World Cup against Spain was a turning point for his nation. It's extremely uncommon for a full-back to win one of these awards, but credit must be given when someone who owns their position as much as Mendes.

12. Erling Haaland

Although Manchester City didn't win the Premier League or Champions League, it shouldn't be forgotten that they had a successful season by winning the FA Cup and Carabao Cup. Spearheading that was Erling Haaland, who bagged 38 goals in 52 appearances and picked up the Premier League Golden Boot.

‌



But Haaland's goals for Norway deserve as much as acclaim, with his 16 goals in qualifying firing them to the World Cup. The striker the struck seven times in five games at the tournament to rubber stamp that he can do it for both club and country.

11. Fabian Ruiz

He may not be as lauded as Vitinha or Neves, but Fabian Ruiz won a massive four trophies for club and country during the voting period. The Spaniard got his hands on the FIFA Intercontinental Cup, Ligue 1, the Champions League and World Cup.

Ruiz isn't always a starter for his teams but his contribution can't be overlooked. It's time for him to no longer be the unsung hero of the PSG engine room.

10. Lionel Messi

Into the top 10 now and regardless of how you rate Lionel Messi now that he plays in Major League Soccer, he's bound to get votes after a dazzling World Cup with Argentina. Scoring eight goals and providing four assists at the tournament showed that he's far from finished, although he recently retired from international football in the wake of Argentina's defeat in the final.

‌



Messi provided two assists as Inter Miami won MLS Cup for the first time in December, and - not that they all should count for the Ballon d'Or - he's contributed to a whopping 32 goals in 24 games for his club in 2026. Incredible for a 39-year-old.

View 7 Images Lionel Messi is still going strong as a veteran (Image: Robin Alam/ISI Photos)

9. Pau Cubarsi

It's hard to believe but Pau Cubarsi is still only 19. The Barcelona academy graduate has long been one of the first names of the team sheet for Hansi Flick and now has the same standing at international level.

Collecting the Spanish Super Cup, the La Liga title and the World Cup this year, he's already got a trophy cabinet which will be the envy of 99 per cent of footballers. Cubarsi would perhaps get more attention if there wasn't another teenager in Barcelona and Spain's ranks.

‌



8. Declan Rice

It feels like we hear more about what Declan Rice supposedly can't do than rather than all the things he can. But the Arsenal midfielder keeps performing and powering his team to wins week in week out, chipping away at the critics.

Instrumental in Arsenal's Premier League title triumph as well as their runs to the finals of the Carabao Cup and Champions League, his endeavour for England at the World Cup when he evidently wasn't fit also speaks volumes of his character. And after five goals and nine assists last term, don't let anyone tell you he isn't useful going forward.

7. Ousmane Dembele

The reigning champion was the clear favourite going into last year's Ballon d'Or ceremony, but it'd be a shock to see him win it again. Nevertheless, don't let that discredit another fantastic season for Ousmane Dembele.

With 20 goals and 11 assists to his name, the Frenchman proved that he's now one of Europe's most consistent attackers after years of debate over whether he was reliable enough to win the biggest prizes. Dembele did that again with PSG, although fell short with France.

‌



View 7 Images Ousmane Dembele won the Ballon d'Or last year (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

6. Michael Olise

The numbers speak for themselves with Michael Olise. In 52 games, the winger managed 23 goals and 26 assists in a team where he isn't even the star forward - more on him later, though.

Olise's remarkable output earned him the Bundesliga Player of the Year award as Bayern Munich stormed to the title before winning the German Cup. The ex-Crystal Palace man also finished the World Cup with the most assists (seven).

5. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia

Despite not featuring at the World Cup, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia should absolutely be a top contender for the Ballon d'Or. Two-footed, tenacious and a scorer of crucial goals, there are few players better to watch than the Georgian.

‌



Kvaratskhelia scored in every knockout round of the Champions League barring the final, including a sensational 28-minute appearance against Chelsea which saw him score two goals and create another. A breathtaking player to watch and for full-backs to handle.

4. Rodri

It's testament to how important Rodri was to Manchester City that only when he was fully fit did they look like they could challenge Arsenal for the Premier League title. His displays in the spring helped close the gap, powering City to two trophies in the process.

For Spain, he pulled the levers in Luis de la Fuente's well-oiled machine. Rodri won the World Cup Golden Ball after another monstrous performance in the final and his move to Barcelona has made them favourites for the Champions League for many.

View 7 Images Rodri was awarded player of the tournament at the World Cup (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

‌



3. Kylian Mbappe

Onto the podium places now and it seems that Kylian Mbappe is running his own campaign to win the Ballon d'Or. After scoring 42 goals in 44 games for Real Madrid, the striker netted 10 for France at the World Cup and broke the tournament's all-time goalscoring record.

"I've made history in the most important competition, Mbappe stated at a press conference this week. "Maybe it's a good year for this but people can vote according to what they think."

There's no doubt that Mbappe will be popular with voters, but his lack of a trophy is expected to harm his chances. The same can't be said of our next two, though.

2. Lamine Yamal

Last year's runner-up, Lamine Yamal may have to settle for the same spot this time around. Spectacular for Barcelona, Yamal scored a career-best 24 goals while providing 17 assists to help Flick's men win a domestic double.

‌



And while the 19-year-old had a quiet World Cup by his standards, he was still ever present for Spain beyond their opening game when he was still recovering from injury. Yamal will have plenty of opportunities to win the Ballon d'Or later in his career, but for now we think he'll have to settle for second.

1. Harry Kane

View 7 Images Harry Kane is the favourite to win the 2026 Ballon d'Or (Image: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images)

Record breaker, history maker, Harry Kane is at the peak of his powers. The headline of his season may've been his 61 goals in 51 games for Bayern, but there's far more to Kane's game than numbers.

Whether it be tracking back to make tackles or spraying passes from midfield, England's captain has got so much in his locker. And it feels fitting that with the Ballon d'Or ceremony due to be held in London for its 70th anniversary, Kane should be there one holding at the end of the night.

‌

Sports.title: Gurney called up to World Series of Darts after withdrawals due to visa issues
Sports.content:
Daryl Gurney has been called up to play at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam after visa issues led to the withdrawal of Philippines players Lourence Ilagan and Alexis Toylo from the September 17-20 event.

Northern Ireland's Gurney and the Netherlands' Maik Kuivenhoven were the highest-ranked players on the reserve list and have replaced Ilagan and Toylo respectively after the pair did not receive a decision on their Schengen visa applications before having to travel to China this week for the final two events of the PDC Asian Tour season.

Gurney will face reigning tournament champion and home favourite Michael van Gerwen in the first round at AFAS Live on Thursday September 17, while Kuivenhoven plays Jonny Clayton the following day.

Luke Littler, the 2024 champion who was beaten 11-7 by Van Gerwen in last year's final, heads to Amsterdam aiming to keep his bid for the first-ever clean sweep of majors in one year on track.

The world champion plays Danny Noppert in round one.

Sports.title: Doyle: Waardah the one to beat in the Park Hill
Sports.content:
Our ambassador Hollie Doyle gives her verdict on the action from Town Moor, providing her take on the Park Hill, May Hill and Sales Race.

Burrows holds key to 'fillies' Leger'

The race they call the Fillies' Leger, the Betfred Park Hill Fillies' Stakes (3.00), is one of the highlights of the opening day of the Betfred St Leger Festival at Doncaster on Thursday and I expect a competitive renewal to go the way of the Owen Burrows-trained Waardah.

She has run two big races in a light campaign in pattern company this year, including in the Group Two Lillie Langtry Stakes at the Qatar Goodwood Festival, only to pay the price for a touch of freshness early in the race - her first since May.

With a hood fitted for the first time, she can prove too good for some classy types including Fairy Glen who shone out in Meydan in the spring when taking the Dubai Gold Cup over two miles from Friday's probable Doncaster Cup favourite Caballo De Mar.

Image: Waardah, ridden by jockey Callum Rodriguez, on their way to winning the Lillie Langtry at Glorious Goodwood

Simon and Ed Crisford's mare has proven form on the back of a break so shouldn't be troubled by a four-month absence and her stamina beyond this extended mile-and-three-quarter trip is assured.

Irish filly looks strong in May Hill

Godolphin's filly Musical Times brings a burgeoning reputation to the other Group Two on the opening day at Doncaster, the Betfred May Hill Stakes (3.35) for the two-year-olds.

Unbeaten in novice races at Newmarket and Yarmouth and on course for a possible crack at the Group One Fillies' Mile, this exciting daughter of Lope De Vega is a fascinating runner in this recognised Classic trial.

However, she hasn't beaten a lot at this stage so I'm taking her on with Irish raider Sea Of Rain, who has already proven herself at a high level with victory in a Group Three at the Curragh last time. Jim Bolger's filly has plenty of experience and won't mind a bit of cut in the ground.

Can't see past Vegas in valuable sales race

I just can't see past the likely favourite Night In Vegas in the big juvenile cavalry charge on the opening day, the Weatherbys £300,000 2-Y-O Stakes (1.50).

Eve Johnson Houghton's colt boasts a lofty rating of 102 yet gets a considerable amount of weight from many of his closest rivals under the terms of this race. His credentials are impeccable with a valuable auction race success at Newmarket last time coming on the back of a creditable third in the Group Two Richmond Stakes at the Goodwood Festival.

I'm hoping to see my husband Tom (Marquand) go well on William Haggas's God Given Talent who was unlucky in running when fourth in a hot nursery at York's Ebor Festival on his first start for the yards since leaving James Ferguson.

Satellite Of Love, who like God Given Talent has a rating of 91, can also play a part. Clive Cox's colt was unbeaten in his first two starts before finishing a well beaten fifth behind the thrown-in Group One winner Sun Goddess in that York sales race.

Cox filly can make winning nursery debut

Art Of Life is yet to get her head in front but can make a winning debut out of novice company in the British Stallion Studs 'Carrie Red' EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap (1.15) on Thursday.

Cox's filly has been unlucky to bump into a couple of promising types at Newbury, including when a shade too keen behind Tom's hot favourite Sweetwonderfulyou last time.

I marginally prefer her to Richard Spencer's likely favourite Speed Of Sound, a lovely Sioux Nation filly who ran a stormer at the weights behind Sun Goddess in that valuable sales race at York.

At a much bigger price, Richard Hannon's Rollthedicebaby has the talent to get back on track off an easing mark after finishing in the pack behind Speed Of Sound on the Knavesmire.

King can reign back in handicap grade

Tom and his boss William have the one they all have to beat in the mile and a quarter Pertemps Network Handicap (2.25) on the opening day.

King Of Earth impressed me when taking a valuable Curragh handicap in the summer in first time cheekpieces and can be forgiven his effort last time in Group Three company at York.

Back in a handicap with the ground and a good draw in his favour, he can get quickly back on track at the possible expense of John and Thady Gosden's Runman.

It's early days for the son of Frankel who put a two-month break behind him to win over this trip at Newbury last time. He looks very well treated off just a three-pound higher mark and will enjoy conditions on Town Moor.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

Watch every race of the Betfred St Leger Festival live on Sky Sports Racing (Sky 415 | Virgin 512) from Thursday 10th to Sunday 13th September.

Sports.title: Merson: Arsenal didn't make X-factor signing to win Champions League
Sports.content:
Arsenal's record last year was amazing in the Champions League and they're going to be there or thereabouts again – but I don't think they bought that X factor signing to take them to that next level.

They have enough to win the Premier League with their squad. I just think the forward line against the big boys, they're missing that little ingredient.

If they'd had a Vinicius Junior or a Julian Alvarez, that would have given them the edge to go on and win the Champions League.

I think they might just fall short.

I'm a big fan of Kai Havertz. He does a lot of work and he's what I call a good footballer. He works hard and makes the right decisions. I just think he's not going to score 20 goals in a season. To take them to the Premier League title, there's no doubt about it, he's a top-drawer player.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at some of Kai Havertz's best goals in the Premier League.

The other thing I look at is when Arsenal go and play against Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain, teams like that in the Champions League latter stages, the centre-halves and the full-backs, getting up in the morning and going to their team talk and saying to one of the other players, "Didn't sleep very well last night, a bit worried about who I'm playing against".

I don't see that for Arsenal. Maybe Bukayo Saka for the left-back, but they haven't got that X factor.

I think that's what they found out in the final last year. Arsenal had no pace getting forward, and PSG just squeezed the game up and didn't let Arsenal out of their half. That would be the worry.

They had been so close to winning the Premier League and then they got over the line, I wouldn't say comfortably, but they've kicked on again.

They've got some good players. I think they could have gone on again and bought a real, real superstar. But their squad is immense. It's so solid.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arsenal head coach Mikel Arteta says they are prepared for the start of their Champions League campaign against Napoli.

It's so hard just to get a shot off against them, let alone score a goal. Chelsea went there with one of the best, if not the best, front threes in the Premier League.

They scored after 77 seconds, but I can't remember them ever looking like they'd score another goal after that. So that just shows you how dominant Arsenal are at the moment.

It's important you start well in the Champions League. When the tournament changed to this format, teams struggled. They had eight games, they thought they'd win enough and get through. Manchester City and Paris Saint-Germain struggled at times to get through.

And then last year, everybody tried to get their wins under their belt very, very quickly. This is an important game tonight. They'll want to keep the momentum going.

If you'd said to me a year or two ago, Napoli away, I'd have said it was a hard game. But Chelsea went there in Europe and beat them and they hadn't been beaten for a long time at home. So they're beatable and I don't expect Arsenal to lose.

Sports.title: Men’s Ballon d’Or 2026 power rankings: will there be an English winner for the first time in 25 years?
Sports.content:
1) Harry Kane (England/Bayern Munich)

Even adjusting for the goal-drunken Bundesliga, his 61 goals in 51 matches for Bayern last season undersells his all-around impact, considering his playmaking and hold-up skills. Kane was gameplanned out of England’s later games at the World Cup, but he was unstoppable through the last 16 to close out the finest year of his career to date. If not now, when?

2) Rodri (Spain/Manchester City – now at Barcelona)

He boasts a comparable case to when he won this prize in 2024 – Rodri remains the epicenter of an incredibly effective Spanish collective. This time around, there’s no Premier League glory to bolster his hopes, as City’s late challenge fizzled out with the club “only” winning domestic cups in his final season at the Etihad. Back to his best en route to Spain’s second World Cup title, though only one of the four previous World Cup champions had the corresponding Ballon d’Or winner (Lionel Messi, 2023).

3) Kylian Mbappé (France/Real Madrid)

Mbappé and José Mourinho have launched an aggressive campaign for the Frenchman to win his first Ballon d’Or. He was even more difficult to slow in his second Spanish season, with 40 goals in 42 matches across La Liga and the Champions League; the less said about his pressing, the better. Few players captivated and dominated like Mbappé at the World Cup, as he won the Golden Boot. But a lack of team accomplishments could set back his candidacy, made even more glaring given Madrid’s chronic success.

4) Lamine Yamal (Spain/Barcelona)

Another member of the World Cup champions, although injuries limited his impact in North America – the master of suspense was not as involved as he’d have liked. Then again, he managed greater consistency in his third season as a regular for Barcelona, with 41 goal contributions in all competitions across 45 appearances. He only just turned 19 in July.

5) Lionel Messi (Argentina/Inter Miami)

Messi could well have ranked higher had Argentina won the World Cup this summer, as the 39-year-old was the heart and soul of their campaign. Alas, a putrid final showing (by his teammates, more than Messi) dulls the sheen on his hopes for a ninth Ballon d’Or, and he is also hit by the fact that he doesn’t play for one of Europe’s elite clubs, even though Inter Miami won the MLS title. His remarkable 17th appearance on a Ballon d’Or shortlist is well deserved.

6) Michael Olise (France/Bayern Munich)

Who knew Bayern’s most thrilling attack in recent memory would be spearheaded by signings from Tottenham and Crystal Palace? An elite secondary attacker, and one who has come to relish operating as the string-puller in transition and at the edge of the final third. Spain masterfully closed his passing lines and took him out of the semi-final, but a pair of assists in the third-place match put him top in that category at the World Cup. A career year, or evidence he’s set a new standard for himself?

7) Erling Haaland (Norway/Manchester City)

Even as City stumbled down the stretch, this was another season to pad his growing legacy as one of the game’s great strikers of any era. He made the most of Norway’s return to the World Cup, finishing as the tournament’s joint-third top goalscorer (seven) despite exiting in the quarter-final.

8) Jude Bellingham (England/Real Madrid)

Birmingham City’s decision to retire his number when his career had barely started has aged well. A man for the big moments, he forged a rare tandem with Kane at the World Cup, alternating headline hero shifts en route to another semi-final heartbreaker. His goals and assists plummeted in his third season with Madrid, though most of his teammates saw diminishing returns in a forgettable campaign.

9) Ousmane Dembélé (France/Paris Saint-Germain)

Lacking some of the bombast that typifies his rivals, Dembélé remains a silky threat for club and country. His stats for PSG dipped from last year’s award-winning campaign, from 35 goals in 53 games to 20 in 40. His partnership with Mbappé and Olise for France was as dangerous as the international game has seen. If nothing else, Dembélé has made certain that he is no one-year wonder.

10) Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (Georgia/Paris Saint-Germain)

On a per-minute basis, few players are more effective in the biggest games. Unfortunately, his club’s domestic dominance means he can take more shifts off than most of his gilded peers, logging a measly 1,479 Ligue 1 minutes in 28 appearances. Georgia’s absence from this summer’s World Cup also limits the evidence available to bolster his case. Nonetheless, his barnstorming exploits in the Champions League knockouts saw the 25-year-old hit rare form.

11) Declan Rice (England/Arsenal)

The most vital cog in Mikel Arteta’s meticulous machine, and a key all-around impact in England’s run to the World Cup semi-final, even if he at times understandably looked tired after a long domestic campaign.

12) Bruno Fernandes (Portugal/Manchester United)

One of a few Portuguese players whose cases for this prize were scuppered by this summer’s underwhelming showing under the stubborn Roberto Martínez. Truly sensational to restore the Red Devils to prouder days.

13) Pau Cubarsí (Spain/Barcelona)

Looked every part the lead center-back that his club and country need to play in a possession-dominant way. Then again, these prizes seldom skew towards defenders.

14) Fabián Ruiz (Spain/Paris Saint-Germain)

Success in the Champions League and World Cup has seen this fine facilitator get his due at age 30.

15) Vitinha (Portugal/Paris Saint-Germain)

Involved in PSG’s best stuff no matter the competition, with six of his seven club goals coming in the Champions League last season. Unable to shed the stench of Portugal’s World Cup, but he is the world’s finest deep-lying playmaker all the same.

16) Luis Díaz (Colombia/Bayern Munich)

Took to Germany with glee, bagging 26 goals and 19 assists in 51 appearances to dwarf his output at Liverpool. Struggled for most of the World Cup, however, as Colombia crashed out sooner than expected.

17) Gabriel (Brazil/Arsenal)

Always close to any fracas, Gabriel was steady as ever as Arsenal enjoyed a long-awaited Premier League title. Some great summer showings at the World Cup, especially against Japan, but struggled – like the rest of his team – against Norway.

18) Nuno Mendes (Portugal/Paris Saint-Germain)

Few opponents have found how to best neutralize Mendes, save for hoping that PSG give him another domestic day off between Champions League games.

19) Lautaro Martínez (Argentina/Inter)

Another dependable goalscoring campaign in Italy, and excelled in a super-sub role during Argentina’s knockout run. One of this era’s great strikers, and already off to a hot start this season.

20) William Saliba (France/Arsenal)

Especially steady in the Premier League and Champions League, helping Arsenal to their most successful year in decades. His injury hurt France’s chances against Spain in the World Cup semi-final, perhaps bolstering his reputation in absentia.

And the rest of the field …

21) Achraf Hakimi (Morocco/Paris Saint-Germain)

22) Vinícius Júnior (Brazil/Real Madrid)

23) Dayot Upamecano (France/Bayern Munich)

24) Marc Cucurella (Spain/Chelsea – now at Real Madrid)
