The President-General subsequently took the floor.

“Now that the House has mandated me to speak, I will now speak,” Archbishop Kawas declared.

The leader of the Charismatic Bishops, who said the CBCN had more than 950 consecrated and installed canonical bishops in Nigeria and maintained a presence in 51 countries, expressed support for the administration of President Tinubu.

Don’t turn security crisis into religious war – Minister

Earlier, Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, urged religious leaders to use their influence to promote peace, responsible citizenship and national unity, particularly as the country approaches the 2027 elections.

Idris said Nigerians had the constitutional right to support any political party or candidate regardless of religious affiliation, while religious leaders were equally entitled to hold political opinions.

“Political competition is part of democracy. Nigerians have the right to support the political party or candidate of their choice, regardless of their religious affiliation. Religious leaders also have the right, as citizens, to hold political opinions,” he said.

He, however, warned against allowing political contests to assume religious or ethnic dimensions, insisting that Nigeria’s security challenges should not be presented as a religious war.

According to him, terrorists and criminal groups had attacked Nigerians of different faiths and backgrounds, with their broader objective being to create fear and undermine national unity.

The minister said the Tinubu administration had strengthened intelligence gathering, inter-agency cooperation, military operations, logistics and international security partnerships.

He said approximately 1,000 terrorists, including dozens of their leaders, were eliminated in the North-East during the first quarter of 2026, while 308 abducted Nigerians were rescued in Niger and Kwara states in August in a coordinated operation involving the Armed Forces, Department of State Services and Nigeria Police Force.

Idris urged religious leaders to complement the work of security agencies by promoting social cohesion and steering young people away from radicalisation and criminality.

Economy: ‘The journey to prosperity has begun’

Turning to the economy, Idris said 27 of the 36 states were unable to pay workers’ wages as of May 2023, but argued that the situation had changed significantly under the present administration.

He said foreign reserves had risen above $54 billion, while GDP had increased and headline and food inflation were declining.

Idris also said Nigeria had been cleared by the Financial Action Task Force, FATF, of concerns over money laundering and other illicit financial dealings, describing the development as a boost to international confidence and investment.

He acknowledged that economic reforms had not eliminated the difficulties facing households.

“This does not in any way mean that everything is now perfect. This does not mean that we have reached the destination we want to reach,” he said.

“But the journey to our economic prosperity has begun.”

He defended the removal of the petrol subsidy, saying it had created fiscal headroom for increased investment in infrastructure, while government was also investing in human capital through programmes including the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, 3 Million Technical Talent Programme, Youth Investment Fund, National Youth Talent Export Programme and Student Venture Capital Grant.

The minister urged churches to deepen their involvement in education, healthcare, humanitarian assistance, vocational training and youth development, while encouraging young Nigerians to embrace entrepreneurship, discipline and the dignity of work.

‘Don’t use smartphones to spread misinformation’

Idris also warned against the spread of misinformation through social media, urging Nigerians to verify information before sharing it.

“The laptop, the smartphone and, indeed, every other device that you hold in your hands should aid you to grow and prosper. We should not use these devices to spread misinformation,” Idris said.

He urged religious leaders to use their influence to promote truth, tolerance and responsible citizenship, noting that millions of Nigerians look to pastors, bishops and other religious leaders for guidance on issues beyond religion.

2027: ‘No election should divide Nigerians’

On the 2027 elections, Idris urged religious leaders to encourage Nigerians to examine candidates’ records and programmes, vote according to their conscience and accept legitimate electoral outcomes.

“No election should be allowed to turn Christian against Muslim or Muslim against Christian, North against South or one ethnic group against another,” he said.

He reaffirmed the government’s commitment to freedom of thought, conscience and religion, stressing that Christians, Muslims and adherents of other faiths must be free to practise their beliefs.

Idris commended the CBCN for promoting unity among Christians and maintaining relationships with Muslims and people of other faiths, urging the organisation to deepen its contribution to national development.

He said citizens did not have to like the government or its leaders but had a responsibility to preserve the unity of Nigeria.

“You do not necessarily have to like the government. You do not even have to necessarily like those who are leading this country at this point,” Idris said.

“But it is pertinent that, even as you do that, you have a responsibility to preserve and promote the unity of this country.”

He said elections were only moments in the life of a nation and should not be allowed to destroy the larger Nigerian project.

The minister called for greater cooperation among government, religious and traditional leaders, the private sector, professionals, young people and communities in building a peaceful and prosperous Nigeria.

World.title: 2027: INEC plans IDP voting centres in nine Plateau LGs
World.content:
File: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan

121,821 new voters registered in state, 65,928 are women

By Golok Nanmwa

JOS — The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, says it is planning to establish voting centres for Internally Displaced Persons, IDPs, in nine local government areas of Plateau State ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Resident Electoral Commissioner, REC, in the state, Prof. Samuel Egwu, disclosed this on Wednesday at a meeting with leaders of political parties and other stakeholders at the Commission’s headquarters in Jos.

Egwu said the initiative was in line with Nigeria’s obligations under the Kampala Declaration on Internally Displaced Persons, which guarantees displaced citizens the right to participate in elections.

He explained that the Commission was preparing for the possibility that some displaced persons might be unable to return to their communities before the elections.

“We don’t even know what will happen next week, but by the facts that we know now, we may have to prepare for IDP voting in nine local governments out of 17.

“These are Bassa, Barkin Ladi, Riyom, Jos South, Mangu, Kanam, Kanke, Wase and Bokkos,” he said.

According to the REC, where security challenges prevent displaced voters from returning to their communities, INEC would establish voting arrangements at their places of displacement.

He, however, stressed that votes cast by IDPs would be collated and counted as part of their original wards and constituencies.

“Nigeria is a signatory to the Kampala Declaration on internally displaced persons, and that means we signed as a country to do everything possible for everybody, including people displaced from their original homes, to vote during election,” Egwu said.

“Their votes will still be taken to be counted as part of their wards for their taking part in choosing their local leaders in 2027,” he added.

Egwu urged political parties to collaborate with INEC to identify and track displaced persons to facilitate proper documentation ahead of the elections.

“We need to partner with you to identify and to promptly report where your supporters are likely to be displaced, so that we can document them for the purpose of IDP voting.

“It will be costly, but we have to do it because it is part and parcel of the democracy struggle to ensure that those people are capable of voting on election day,” he said.

The REC expressed optimism that peace would return to the affected communities before the 2027 elections, enabling displaced persons to return to their ancestral homes.

“Our prayer is that maybe normalcy will return and people can return to their original abode. But should that not happen, they will have the chance to be able to vote,” he said.

Egwu described the meeting as part of the Commission’s ongoing engagement with political parties, civil society organisations and other stakeholders ahead of the elections.

He said the meeting was taking place 129 days before the 2027 elections, adding that more engagements would be held before election day.

“This is a very timely meeting, and there will be many more between now and the election.

“What we do as an election management body is to provide electoral information and to continue to update you as things change or don’t change,” he said.

The REC said sustained engagement with political parties was essential to the successful conduct of the 2027 elections.

“There is no way we can conduct election in 2027 without talking first and foremost to political parties, because democracy is party politics,” he added.

He explained that civil society organisations were also included because they were “our natural allies” in strengthening democracy.

According to him, “Civil society represents citizens. They do advocacy not about their interest, but about what will improve democracy.”

On the electoral timetable, Egwu said INEC would publish the final list of candidates for the presidential and National Assembly elections on September 12, 2026, while the final list for governorship and State House of Assembly elections would be published on October 10, 2026.

He further disclosed that 121,821 new voters were registered in Plateau State during the last Continuous Voter Registration, CVR, exercise, with females accounting for 65,928.

The Commission also recorded 38,399 requests for voter transfers, while about 95,000 Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs, from previous registration cycles remained uncollected in the state.

Egwu urged political actors to conduct their campaigns with decorum and warned against acts capable of undermining the credibility and peaceful conduct of the electoral process.

World.title: Women dominate new voter registration, lag in elective offices — INEC
World.content:
Commission urges parties to provide greater support for female candidates ahead of 2027

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA — The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, has raised concerns over the wide gap between women’s participation as voters and their representation in elective offices in Nigeria.

The Commission noted that although women accounted for the majority of new registrants in the third phase of the recently concluded Continuous Voter Registration, CVR, their numerical strength at the polling units had yet to translate into commensurate representation in political leadership.

Chairman of INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, stated this on Wednesday at a strategic engagement with political party leaders, female candidates, civil society organisations and development partners in Abuja ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Amupitan, who was represented by National Commissioner, Prof. Rhoda Gumus, disclosed that of the 3,867,997 Nigerians who completed registration in the third phase of the CVR as of July 26, 2026, women accounted for 2,037,589, representing 52.68 per cent, while men accounted for 1,830,408.

Gumus said: “Women therefore accounted for the majority of new registrants in the final phase of the exercise.”

She said the figure was consistent with the pattern recorded during the 2023 general election, when women accounted for 44,414,846 of the 93,469,008 registered voters, representing 47.52 per cent.

According to her, the figures showed that women constituted a substantial part of Nigeria’s electorate.

However, she said the numerical strength had not been reflected in the number of women contesting or winning elective positions.

Citing the 2023 election, Gumus said only 1,556 of the 15,331 candidates across major elective positions were women, representing 10.15 per cent.

She added that only three women were elected to the Senate and 16 to the House of Representatives, representing 2.8 per cent and 4.4 per cent of the respective seats.

“A substantial gap appears to exist between women’s participation as voters and their participation as political leaders,” she said.

Gumus added: “A democracy that mobilises women as voters but provides limited pathways for them to become political leaders is yet to fully realise its representative potential.”

She urged political parties to provide practical support to female candidates, including access to party structures and leadership, campaign platforms, media visibility, fundraising networks, mentoring, political communication, logistics, security and grassroots mobilisation.

She also challenged parties to examine whether women were being given genuine opportunities to rise through their ranks.

“The participation of women is not a favour to women. It is a democratic imperative,” she said, urging political parties to move “from commitment to action, from aspiration to implementation.”

In a welcome address delivered on her behalf by the Director, Gender and Inclusivity Department, Lakunuya Dorothy Bello, the Secretary to the Commission, Dr Rose Oriaran-Anthony, said advancing women’s political participation could not be achieved by INEC or any single institution alone.

She called for collective commitment and sustained action by all stakeholders, stressing that political parties, as the principal vehicles through which citizens organise and seek elective office, had a direct responsibility for creating opportunities for women.

According to her, the policies, structures and internal processes of political parties significantly influence who contests and ultimately wins elections.

Delivering the keynote address, titled, “Strengthening Women’s Political Participation and Representation: Opportunities, Challenges and Strategies for Political Parties Towards the 2027 General Elections,” a former INEC Director of Voter Education, Publicity, Gender and Civil Societies Liaison and former Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, Edo State, Oluwole Osaze-Uzi, said Nigeria remained one of the countries lagging behind in women’s representation in elected public offices.

Osaze-Uzi said women constituted roughly half of the country’s population and electorate but occupied only about five per cent of seats in the National Assembly.

He also noted that no woman had ever been elected President or governor in Nigeria.

Tracing the history of female presidential candidacy from 1999, when there was no female presidential candidate, to the 2027 election cycle, where three women are among the 14 presidential candidates, he compared Nigeria’s record with that of other African countries that had made significant progress in women’s political representation.

He cited Rwanda, where female parliamentary representation rose from below five per cent in 1994 to nearly 64 per cent, as well as Senegal’s Parity Law of 2010 and voluntary party quota systems in Namibia, South Africa, Mozambique and Cape Verde.

Osaze-Uzi said 41 of the 54 African countries now operated some form of gender quota.

He identified legal, cultural, security, financial and political-will barriers as some of the factors limiting women’s participation in Nigerian politics.

He recommended stronger legal frameworks, enforcement mechanisms within political parties, dedicated campaign funding for women and mentorship programmes.

He also called for zero tolerance for intimidation, threats and sexual harassment of female candidates.

“The evidence also shows how much can also be achieved even with voluntary quotas where there is a strong commitment and political will,” he said.

World.title: Lassa fever: NCDC urges Nigerians to step up prevention
World.content:
Lassa fever

Warns cases typically rise between November and April

By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja

ABUJA — The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, has urged Nigerians to intensify preventive measures against Lassa fever ahead of the dry season, warning that cases typically increase between November and April.

The Director-General of the NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, gave the warning on Wednesday in Abuja at a national health security media briefing, stressing the need for early preparedness before the peak transmission period.

Idris said although Lassa fever occurs throughout the year, cases tend to increase during the dry season, making the period before the peak season critical for prevention and preparedness.

“Lassa fever occurs throughout the year, but cases tend to increase during the dry season, particularly between November and April. We are not yet in that peak period, and that gives us an important opportunity to act now,” he said.

The NCDC said findings from its After Action Review of the last Lassa fever outbreak showed persistent gaps in early care-seeking, infection prevention and control, environmental sanitation, state-level preparedness and the functionality of health facilities.

According to the agency, delays in seeking appropriate medical care, self-treatment and visits to multiple health facilities before Lassa fever was suspected contributed to challenges in managing cases.

It also identified infections among healthcare workers, particularly when health facilities were under pressure, as well as environmental and household risks associated with poor sanitation, unsafe food storage and exposure to rodents.

Idris said the findings underscored the need to strengthen the entire response chain, from prevention and early detection to diagnosis, referral and treatment.

He disclosed that the NCDC had developed an Accelerated Readiness Plan to guide preparedness activities ahead of the peak Lassa fever season.

“Our approach during this period will be firmly grounded in One Health. Lassa fever cannot be prevented and controlled by the health sector acting alone. Health, Environment, Agriculture, Livestock, Local Governments and communities have distinct but complementary responsibilities,” he said.

According to him, the plan will focus on measures to be implemented between now and the peak season, with additional attention and resources directed to areas where available data indicate that the burden and risk are highest.

Under the plan, the agency said priority would be given to early detection and reporting of suspected cases, reducing exposure to rodents, promoting prompt care-seeking and ensuring healthcare workers can recognise, report and appropriately refer suspected cases.

It added that efforts would be made to ensure prompt transportation and testing of samples, as well as timely communication of results to healthcare providers.

The NCDC urged households to store food items such as rice, garri, beans and maize in tightly covered containers and avoid leaving food exposed to rodents.

It also advised Nigerians to seal openings through which rodents could enter homes, reduce clutter that provides hiding places for rodents and maintain clean surroundings through proper waste disposal.

The agency cautioned against handling rodents with bare hands or unnecessary contact with their urine, faeces and other body fluids.

It further advised people who develop fever or other symptoms, particularly those living in or travelling to areas where Lassa fever is endemic, to seek medical attention promptly.

“If you have treated what you believe to be malaria and your symptoms persist, please do not continue treating yourself at home. Seek appropriate medical attention,” the agency advised.

The NCDC also called on state and local governments, particularly those with recurrent Lassa fever transmission, to strengthen environmental sanitation, waste management, surveillance, laboratory referral systems and the readiness of designated treatment centres.

It urged health authorities to investigate every Lassa fever infection involving a healthcare worker, appropriately follow up exposed workers and promptly address identified gaps.

The agency urged healthcare workers to remain vigilant, saying: “THINK LASSA. PROTECT. REPORT. REFER.”

World.title: Photos: Remi Tinubu bags Oso Di Eme I chieftaincy title in Imo
World.content:
ABUJA — First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, has been conferred with the traditional title of Oso Di Eme I of Imo State.

The honour was announced on Wednesday by the First Lady’s Senior Special Adviser on Media, Busola Kukoyi, in a statement accompanied by photographs of the ceremony posted on her X handle.

Kukoyi said the title, which she translated as “she who supports her husband,” was in recognition of the First Lady’s role as a partner to President Bola Tinubu in the administration of the country.

She wrote: “Oso Di Eme I of Imo State, meaning ‘She who supports her husband.’ A worthy partner of her husband, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR. As he’s working, she is working.”

Photographs released by the aide showed the First Lady dressed in colourful traditional attire featuring APC symbols and Nigerian flag motifs.

She was also seen wearing a red headwrap and coral beads, while holding a ceremonial fan inscribed “OSO DI EME” and a white horsetail flywhisk.

The conferment took place during the First Lady’s visit to Imo State, where she was received by traditional rulers.

The honour comes months after she was conferred with the chieftaincy title of Ugosimba I of Enugu in June 2026.

The Enugu title, which translates as “Jewel of Empowerment” in Igbo, was conferred in recognition of her efforts towards women’s empowerment and social development across the country.

World.title: SEDC to prioritise poultry development in South-East
World.content:
Urges youths to embrace agriculture

By Anayo Okoli

ENUGU — The South East Development Commission (SEDC) has pledged to prioritise the development of the poultry industry in the region as part of efforts to unlock its agricultural potential, boost food security and create jobs.

The Managing Director of SEDC, Mark Okoye Jnr., disclosed this at the Eastern International Poultry Summit 2026, organised by the Poultry Association of Nigeria (PAN), South-East zone, in Enugu.

Okoye, who was represented by the commission’s Executive Director, Natural Resources, Agriculture and Rural Development, Dr Cliff Ogbede, said the development of poultry farming would enhance nutrition, catalyse economic growth and create thousands of jobs in the region.

Speaking on the theme, “From Farm to Market: Scaling Nigeria’s Poultry Trade and Investment,” Ogbede said poultry was one of the sectors the commission would devote resources to in its drive to position the South-East as a leading producer of poultry products in Nigeria.

He expressed concern over the region’s dependence on other parts of the country for livestock and food despite its vast agricultural potential.

Ogbede recalled that the administration of the late Dr Michael Okpara, Premier of the former Eastern Region, leveraged agriculture and other sectors to accelerate economic development in the 1950s and 1960s.

According to him, the SEDC intends to draw lessons from that era while adapting its development blueprint to current economic realities.

He said experts had been engaged to study and modernise Okpara’s development strategy, with emphasis on agriculture, livestock production, value addition and private-sector investment.

Ogbede said poultry development would be a major focus of the commission’s agricultural intervention.

“I am proud to tell you today that poultry development is one area that the SEDC will spend time and money to support.

“If you see the records of how much we send out of this region monthly just to buy cows and poultry products, you will know that we are in big trouble,” he said.

He identified high feed costs, climate-related challenges and dependence on other regions for inputs as some of the factors undermining poultry production in the South-East.

According to him, the region risks serious food and economic challenges if it continues to depend heavily on livestock and poultry products from other parts of the country.

Ogbede also said the region was not meeting its nutritional potential through agriculture, stressing the need to increase local production and improve access to affordable food.

He said the establishment of regional development commissions had created an opportunity for different parts of the country to compete in economic development.

“In the South-East, we should do our best to reclaim our status as a region with the fastest-growing economic potential,” he said.

The SEDC executive director further said several development partners had expressed willingness to support farmers in the region through capacity building, blended financing and improved market access.

He, however, said some partners had raised concerns about the tendency of people and organisations in the region to operate in silos rather than collaborate.

Ogbede urged youths in the South-East to embrace agriculture instead of relocating to Lagos, Abuja and other cities in search of employment.

“Agriculture is a big business,” he said, citing the Netherlands as an example of how a relatively small landmass could generate significant economic value from agriculture.

He said the SEDC would also focus on rebuilding infrastructure destroyed during the civil war, tackling erosion and addressing climate-related challenges as part of its broader development mandate.

“We are going to do a lot in agriculture. Our children should feed and our food should have enough nutritional value. We must also be intentional in making money from agriculture in our environment,” Ogbede said.

He assured PAN that the commission would collaborate with the association to achieve tangible results in the poultry sector.

Earlier, National Vice President of PAN, Sir Izuolisa Onu, said the South-East was once the largest poultry hub in Nigeria before losing its position to the South-West.

Onu said the association had begun discussions on how to revive the sector and use it as a catalyst for economic growth and job creation in the region.

He expressed satisfaction with the participation of the SEDC and state governments at the summit, saying the discussions would focus on practical measures to make the poultry industry more impactful.

Also speaking, a former adviser to the United States Department of Agriculture, Uche Nzeka, called for the development of a comprehensive poultry strategy for the South-East.

Nzeka said the strategy should address the challenges confronting poultry farmers and promote an integrated commercial value chain for the industry.

He proposed the establishment of an integrated poultry value-chain company, to be known as Oriental Integrated Poultry Limited.

The summit was attended by the President of the Enugu Chamber of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture, Nnanyelugo Onyemelukwe; former Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Toby Okechukwu; senior officials of the SEDC; commissioners from Anambra and Imo states; representatives of the Enugu State Government; and PAN chairmen from the five South-East states and Abuja.

World.title: NAICOM, NCAA strengthen aviation insurance oversight
World.content:
…Set up joint committee on compliance, information sharing

By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

ABUJA — The National Insurance Commission (NAICOM) and the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding, MoU, to strengthen insurance regulation and compliance in Nigeria’s aviation industry.

The agreement, signed in Abuja yesterday by the Commissioner for Insurance and Chief Executive Officer of NAICOM, Olusegun Omosehin, and the Director-General of the NCAA, Capt. Chris Najomo, is expected to enhance passenger protection, improve regulatory compliance and boost investor confidence in the sector.

The MoU establishes a framework for closer collaboration between the two agencies in the oversight of aviation insurance and enforcement of statutory requirements.

Speaking at the signing ceremony, Omosehin described the agreement as a major milestone in institutional cooperation between the regulators, noting that although their statutory responsibilities were distinct, they were complementary in safeguarding the integrity and resilience of the aviation sector.

He said the partnership would provide a coordinated framework for compliance monitoring, risk protection, information sharing and stakeholder engagement, thereby strengthening confidence among airlines, insurers, financiers, aircraft lessors, passengers and other industry stakeholders.

According to him, aviation occupies a strategic position in the Nigerian economy, facilitating commerce, tourism, investment and national development, making effective insurance protection indispensable.

Omosehin said adequate insurance coverage remained a critical risk-management tool for protecting lives, property, businesses and the wider economy.

He explained that under the new arrangement, NAICOM would provide technical support and regulatory oversight on aviation insurance matters, including verification of insurance policies and confirmation of licensed insurers authorised to underwrite aviation risks.

A major component of the agreement is the establishment of a Joint Technical Committee to drive its implementation.

Omosehin said the committee would facilitate information sharing between the agencies, periodically review insurance requirements in the aviation industry, address operational challenges, coordinate stakeholder engagements and organise capacity-building programmes for regulators and industry operators.

He assured the NCAA of NAICOM’s commitment to providing the technical expertise required for the effective functioning of the committee.

The commissioner added that the partnership would promote joint training programmes, exchange of regulatory information and periodic assessment of insurance cover maintained by aviation operators.

He said the measures would improve regulatory effectiveness and deepen confidence in Nigeria’s aviation insurance framework.

Omosehin noted that the success of the MoU would depend on sustained engagement, mutual trust and a shared commitment to regulatory excellence by both institutions.

He said the collaboration went beyond regulatory compliance, stressing that it was fundamentally aimed at protecting policyholders, air travellers and third parties, while strengthening investor confidence in the aviation industry.

The NAICOM boss said compulsory aviation liability insurance provided critical financial protection by ensuring that legitimate claims arising from accidents and other liabilities could be settled, thereby promoting public confidence in air transportation, facilitating access to finance and supporting business continuity.

He added that a strong insurance framework would contribute to the Federal Government’s aspiration of building a $1 trillion economy by supporting investment, enterprise development and long-term economic growth through effective risk management.

Also speaking, NCAA Director-General, Najomo, said the agreement underscored the shared commitment of both agencies to strengthening the safety, integrity and resilience of Nigeria’s aviation ecosystem.

He said enhanced cooperation between the aviation and insurance regulators would improve compliance, deepen stakeholder confidence and ensure that Nigeria’s aviation industry remained aligned with applicable international conventions and global best practices.

Najomo added that effective collaboration between the institutions would safeguard passengers, protect third parties, support stable aviation operations and promote a safer, more resilient and trusted air transport system.

He said, “As Nigeria pursues the attainment of a one trillion-dollar economy ($1 trillion economy by 2030) under the Renewed Hope Agenda, effective risk management and strong insurance protection must remain key enablers of investment, enterprise, consumer protection, and long-term national development.”

World.title: Army Redeploys Theatre Commander Abubabar, 14 Other Generals in Minor Shake-up
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian Army has redeployed the Theatre Commander of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai, Major General Abdulsalam Abubakar, and 14 other generals in a minor shake-up as part of efforts to enhance operational effectiveness, strengthen leadership and align the service’s command structure with Nigeria’s evolving security environment.

According to a statement by the Acting Director of Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, the Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has approved the strategic redeployment of senior officers to key command, operational and staff appointments across the Nigerian Army.

The exercise, she said, prioritises critical operational theatres and strategic appointments to ensure that the right leadership, experience and expertise are positioned to deliver decisive effects.

“In the new postings, Major General IA Ajose moves from Army Headquarters (AHQ), Department of Army Operations, to the Theatre Command, Joint Task Force (JTF) North-East, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), as Theatre Commander, while Major General AE Abubakar has been redeployed from OPHK to the Nigerian Army Heritage and Future Centre (NAHFC) as Dean, Faculty of Operational Research.

“Major General AM Alechenu moves from Defence Headquarters (DHQ) Garrison to the Nigerian Army Heritage and Future Centre, while Major General RT Utsaha moves from the AHQ Department of Army Standards and Evaluation to DHQ Garrison as Commander.

“Similarly, Major General AM Umar moves from the AHQ Department of Civil-Military Affairs (DCMA) to the Army War College Nigeria (AWCN) as Commandant, while Major General UM Alkali moves from AWCN to AHQ DCMA.

“Major General GS Muhammed moves from the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) to the Nigerian Army Finance Corporation (NAFIC) as Director-General, while Major General JE Osifo moves from NAFIC to the Military Pension Board (MPB) as Chairman. Major General IE Ekpenyong has been redeployed to the DHQ Department of Defence Logistics as Director, Engineering Services.

“At the operational level, Brigadier General AA Bello moves from 6 Division Garrison/Sector 3 JTF South-South, Operation Delta Safe, to the DHQ Department of Defence Operations.

“Brigadier General MS Adamu has been redeployed from the Nigerian Army Women Command to the newly established 8 Brigade as Commander, while Brigadier General MS Sule moves from Special Task Force Operation Enduring Peace to 27 Task Force Brigade as Commander.

“Similarly, Brigadier General I Sule has been redeployed from the Directorate of Recruitment Management to 6 Division Garrison as Commander, while Brigadier General E Azenda moves from the Land Forces Simulation Centre to 2 Division Garrison as Commander. Brigadier General AS Bugaje moves from 2 Division Garrison to the Land Forces Simulation Centre as Director, Administration,” the statement said.

The COAS charged the newly appointed officers to justify the confidence reposed in them through exemplary leadership, operational innovation, professionalism and an unwavering commitment to duty, while remaining relentlessly focused on the constitutional mandate of defending Nigeria’s sovereignty, protecting its territorial integrity and supporting civil authorities in maintaining peace and security.

Colonel Anele said the Nigerian Army remained resolute in sustaining a dynamic leadership and force-employment framework that enhances operational outcomes, strengthens joint and inter-agency coordination, and improves the service’s capacity to respond decisively to contemporary and emerging threats in furtherance of Nigeria’s national security objectives.

World.title: Education Minister Threatens Sack, Licence Withdrawal Over Accreditation Fraud
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has warned heads of tertiary institutions against compromising the integrity of accreditation exercises, saying officials who manipulate the process risk losing their jobs while private institutions could have their licences revoked.

Alausa issued the warning on Wednesday in Abuja at the inauguration of the Ministerial Committee on Strengthening the Accreditation and Quality Assurance System for Tertiary Institutions.

He said the government would no longer tolerate institutions that present inflated or misleading records of their academic capacity during accreditation exercises, stressing that the quality of graduates produced by Nigerian tertiary institutions must reflect the standards approved by regulatory agencies.

According to him, the consequences of weak accreditation are already evident in the difficulty employers face in finding qualified graduates.

“People say they want to hire engineers. They will have 500 candidates, but they wouldn’t be able to get two, three, four or five qualified applicants. That’s the damage we’re doing to this university.

“But guess what? This Ministry of Education is not going to let this continue. Other presidents, other governments may have allowed this to continue, but we are not going to let this continue,” he said.

The minister also announced that the Federal Government would end the practice whereby institutions temporarily borrow academic staff, equipment and facilities from other institutions to meet accreditation requirements.

His position comes amid the controversy surrounding the accreditation of the Law programme at Atiba University, Oyo State.

In August, the Council of Legal Education imposed a 10-year moratorium on the university’s Law programme, citing inadequate facilities, as well as the admission and graduation of students without the requisite approval.

The development has left the affected students and their parents seeking government intervention, including possible transfers to accredited Law faculties to prevent years of study and financial investments from being lost.

Alausa said accreditation must provide an accurate picture of an institution’s actual and sustainable capacity rather than a temporary representation assembled solely for an accreditation visit.

“An institution should not be able to prepare a temporary picture of itself simply for the purpose of an accreditation visit.

“Sadly, this is what persists in the majority of instances,” he said.

He said the government would tackle the practice of temporarily moving academic and non-academic personnel between institutions or presenting them for accreditation before they are returned to their original institutions.

The same measures, he said, would apply to the temporary movement, borrowing or presentation of laboratory equipment, workshop resources, library materials and other facilities solely for accreditation purposes.

According to the minister, whatever an accreditation team sees and verifies must represent the institution’s genuine and sustainable capacity.

Alausa said the reform was designed to strengthen the credibility, integrity, transparency, efficiency and sustainability of accreditation exercises across universities, polytechnics and colleges of education.

He said the National Universities Commission (NUC), National Board for Technical Education (NBTE) and National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE) had critical responsibilities in protecting the quality of tertiary education.

“An institution should not meet prescribed standards only when the NUC, NBTE or NCCE accreditation team is expected to visit. Those standards should be met every day of the year.

“With a robust digital accreditation platform, much of the institutional information required for accreditation can be continuously maintained and periodically verified.

“Before an accreditation team arrives, the accrediting agency should already have reliable information on institutional staffing, facilities, laboratories, workshops and other equipment.

“The physical visit will remain important, but it should increasingly serve to validate verified data rather than begin the verification process from scratch,” he said.

The minister said the committee’s mandate was not to weaken the existing accreditation system but to modernise and strengthen it through transparent, efficient, evidence-based and difficult-to-manipulate processes.

He directed the committee to develop mechanisms for verifying the authenticity and continuous availability of academic and non-academic staff presented for accreditation.

It is also expected to establish mechanisms for verifying the ownership, functionality, adequacy, accessibility and sustained availability of facilities and equipment presented by institutions.

Alausa said technology would be deployed to transform accreditation from a predominantly manual and periodic exercise into a digital, data-driven and continuously verifiable system.

He called for the use of geospatial mapping, geotagging and appropriate digital identification technologies for physical infrastructure, laboratories, workshops and major equipment.

“Critical equipment presented for accreditation should be capable of being digitally identified and linked to a specific institution and physical location,” he said.

He blamed the situation partly on the tolerance of irregularities under previous administrations but assured Nigerians that the President Bola Tinubu administration would no longer allow such practices to continue.

Responding, Chairman of the Ministerial Committee and former Registrar of the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB), Prof. Is-haq Oloyede, pledged the committee’s commitment to addressing abuses in the accreditation process.

Oloyede said accreditation should not be treated as an exercise for which institutions temporarily prepare, stressing that continuous monitoring was critical to ensuring that standards were maintained beyond accreditation visits.

He said the committee would also examine how regulatory and professional bodies could better integrate their accreditation processes and agree on relevant criteria to prevent situations where students complete programmes but are unable to proceed to professional training or registration.

World.title: Akpabio Challenges Authors of Alleged Anti-North Comment to Produce Evidence
World.content:
* Senate President denies threat to make northerners suffer if Tinubu loses 2027 poll

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Office of the President of the Senate has challenged the authors and promoters of a social media publication attributing an alleged anti-northern statement to Senate President Godswill Akpabio, demanding that they produce evidence or withdraw the claim and apologise publicly.

The Senate President’s Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Hon. Eseme Eyiboh, described the purported statement: “We will make sure northerners suffer from January to May if Tinubu loses the election,” as a fabrication designed to inflame ethnic sentiments ahead of the 2027 general election.

In a statement issued Wednesday, Eyiboh said Akpabio never made the statement and challenged those circulating it to produce the original video or audio recording, authenticated transcript, date, venue and details of the occasion where the Senate President allegedly made the comment.

He said: “There is no video, audio recording, speech, interview, press release, transcript or credible news report in which those words were uttered by him.”

According to him, a photograph carrying words placed beneath it could not constitute evidence of such a serious allegation.

“A photograph carrying words placed beneath it is not evidence; it is merely an allegation wearing typography,” he said.

Eyiboh specifically challenged Mr. Ibrahim Umar Ammar, whom he identified as being associated with the Atiku Abubakar Campaign Organisation and as Coordinator of ADC-NYAF, Kano State, as well as others involved in creating, publishing or circulating the material, to substantiate the allegation.

He urged those behind the publication to identify the occasion, date, venue, journalists and media organisations that purportedly witnessed or reported the alleged statement.

“If Engr. Ammar or anyone else claims merely to have reposted the material rather than originated it, then let him identify the source from whom he obtained it and provide the original publication,” he said.

The Senate President’s spokesman said establishing the chain of publication would help determine those responsible for creating the alleged fabrication, knowingly republishing it as fact or coordinating its dissemination.

He said if no evidence existed, those responsible should withdraw the material, apologise publicly and stop what he described as an attempt to poison Nigeria’s political atmosphere with ethnic propaganda.

Eyiboh argued that the alleged statement was particularly dangerous because of its potential to deepen regional and ethnic divisions at a time the country was approaching another major electoral contest.

“This is not legitimate political opposition. It is calculated incitement designed to manufacture fear, resentment and hostility between northern Nigerians and a national leader from the south,” he said.

He maintained that political parties and candidates should contest elections based on ideas, records, policies and alternative visions rather than through allegedly fabricated quotations capable of threatening national cohesion.

The Senate President’s media aide also dismissed the allegation by pointing to Akpabio’s political relationships and official appointments, which he said cut across regional lines.

He noted that the Senate President’s governing partnership with Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin of Kano, as well as the presence of northerners among senior officials and aides in his office, contradicted attempts to portray Akpabio as hostile to the region.

Among the aides cited was Alhaji Dr Jibril Lawal Tafida, Special Adviser on NGO and Diaspora Matters.

Eyiboh recalled that Akpabio’s emergence as Senate President was supported by prominent northern political leaders and senators and that he defeated his challenger by 63 votes to 46 during the election of presiding officers of the 10th Senate.

He also cited the emergence of Barau as Deputy Senate President on the same day, saying the development demonstrated the cross-regional political partnership at the leadership of the Senate.

The statement further highlighted legislative interventions targeted at northern development under Akpabio’s leadership.

According to Eyiboh, the Senate passed legislation establishing the North-West Development Commission to address infrastructural, economic and security challenges confronting the region.

He also cited the North-Central Development Commission legislation, which was subsequently signed into law, as well as legislation establishing a Federal Polytechnic in Rano, Kano State, and a Federal University of Health Sciences in Tsafe, Zamfara State.

“These are tangible institutional interventions intended to promote education, reconstruction, employment and development across northern communities, not the actions of a leader plotting their suffering,” Eyiboh said.

He further recalled Akpabio’s personal visit to Borno State following devastating floods in Maiduguri, saying the Senate President mobilised the solidarity of the National Assembly for victims of the disaster.

According to him, the Senate contributed N74 million to assist flood victims as part of a combined N174 million intervention by the two chambers of the National Assembly.

Eyiboh also listed legislation on student loans, minimum wage, security, education and economic development among measures passed by the National Assembly, arguing that their benefits were available to Nigerians irrespective of their geopolitical zones.

He warned that freedom of political expression should not be interpreted as a licence to manufacture statements capable of provoking ethnic hostility.

“Political freedom carries political responsibility, particularly in a diverse country where inflammatory falsehoods can have consequences far beyond the electoral contest in which they are deployed,” he said.

The Senate President’s office subsequently appealed to Nigerians not to circulate the disputed publication without first establishing its authenticity.

Eyiboh said a claim of such magnitude could not become credible merely because it had been repeatedly posted, liked or shared on social media.

“Nigerians should therefore refuse to become unwitting transmission belts for this dangerous falsehood. Before sharing it, demand the primary evidence,” he said.

He maintained that the burden of proof rested with those alleging that Akpabio made the statement, arguing that the Senate President could not reasonably be expected to prove that he did not utter words allegedly made at an unidentified location, on an unidentified date and before an unidentified audience.

He said: “The demand is therefore straightforward and categorical: produce the original video, produce the original audio, produce an authenticated transcript, name the occasion, give the date and venue, and identify the media organisations that witnessed or reported the statement.

“If none of these can be produced, admit that the quotation was fabricated, withdraw it immediately and apologise publicly.”

Eyiboh urged political actors to ensure that the 2027 electoral contest remained vigorous but responsible, stressing that parties should interrogate records, challenge policies, expose failures, defend achievements and present competing visions for the country.

He warned against exploiting ethnic sensitivities for electoral advantage, saying Nigeria had already paid a heavy price for political manipulation of its ethnic and regional differences.

“The north is not an electoral weapon. The south is not an enemy. Ethnicity is not campaign ammunition. And Nigeria’s unity must never become collateral damage in anybody’s campaign for power,” he said.

World.title: FG Enrols 16,000 Nigerians in Maiden Digital Training Academy Cohort
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Federal Government has admitted 16,000 Nigerians into the first cohort of the Digital Training Academy (DTA), a free initiative aimed at equipping youths with globally competitive digital skills.

National Coordinator of the Special Projects and Innovation Unit at the Federal Ministry of Education, Adebayo Onibanjo, announced this on Wednesday during a pre-launch media briefing in Abuja.

The national launch is set for September 14, 2026.

Onibanjo said the academy received 72,850 applications from across the 36 states and Federal Capital Territory (FCT) between August 17 and September 1, adding that of that number, 19,699 met the entry requirement and 16,000 were selected.

The DTA is being implemented under the Nigeria Education Digital Infrastructure (NEDI) programme, a key component of the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI).

Training will be delivered via Coursera and Pluralsight. The ministry said the programme aligns with the Renewed Hope Agenda and the Data and Digitalisation pillar of NESRI.

Quoting the Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, Onibanjo described the academy as “the next phase of President Tinubu’s commitment to building a highly skilled workforce”’

He added that the 16,000 learners are just the beginning, noting that the cohort “establishes the foundation, the systems, and the delivery partnerships on which subsequent cohorts will be built”.

The ministry thanked applicants and partners including the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy, YabaTech, NOUN, Coursera and Pluralsight.

World.title: 2027: North-west ADC Guber Candidates Unveil Manifesto, Promise N110,000 Minimum Wage
World.content:
• Vow to tackle insecurity, poverty, out-school-children

• Declare support for Atiku’s promise to restore petrol subsidy

Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The North-west African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidates have signed a compact and unveiled a joint manifesto to tackle insecurity and poverty in the region following the commencement of political campaigns for the 2027 governorship and state Houses of Assembly election.

The candidates also declared their support for the presidential candidate of ADC, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, over his plan to restore petrol subsidy.

They also promised to pay N110,000 minimum wage for workers in the region if elected.

The governorship candidates made the declaration on Wednesday in Abuja following the signing of the Northwest ADC Governorship Candidates’ Compact 2027–2031.

Speaking on behalf of the candidates, the former Attorney General of the Federation (AGF) and the governorship candidate of Kebbi State, Abubakar Malami (SAN), said the signing of the compact was to reorient governance and deliver development

He stated: “We are by this gathering unfolding our regional covenant for security, development and shared prosperity.

“We, the governorship candidates of the African Democratic Congress for Jigawa, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kebbi, Sokoto and Zamfara States, having this day adopted and signed the North-west ADC Governorship Candidates’ Compact 2027–2031, address this declaration directly to the people of the North-west as our Regional Covenant for Security, Development and Shared Prosperity.”

Malami lamented that the region is crisis ridden, adding that over 16,000 lives have been lost on account of insecurity between June 2023 and August 2026, while more than 1,583 kidnapping incidents since January 2023 have taken over 10,000 people from their homes and farms.

He decried that tens of thousands of households have been displaced, and more than 533,000 hectares of farmland in Zamfara and Katsina alone now lie abandoned.

Malami stressed that the region also accounted for 45 per cent of Nigeria’s out-of-school children.

He added: “Insecurity has emptied our farms, and those empty farms have brought hunger, driven our children out of the classroom, and have denied them the education the region requires to dry up the recruitment pool for future banditry, kidnappings and all associated crimes.

“Our commitment is to reorient governance to respond effectively and efficiently to break this vicious cycle of crisis, and restore peace, security and normalcy to our region.

“Our states and local government areas have received over N8.33 trillion in federal allocations between June 2023 and August 2026, and yet these revenues have not translated into accessible transport, affordable food and healthcare, functioning schools, and improved living conditions for our people.”

Malami assured the people that individually and collectively, they would take deliberate measures to reverse this unacceptable reality and ensure that public resources deliver measurable improvements in the lives of our citizens.

He noted: “This is why we commit to reform with responsibility, relief with accountability, and growth our citizens can feel.”

Malami noted that the level of looting witnessed across the North-west under the current administrations is massive and unprecedented in the region.

According to him, “We hold that the APC-led administrations in this region have little or nothing to show for their stewardship, neither in the lives of our people, physical infrastructure nor the security of lives and property.

“Rather than progress, our people are more impoverished today than at any time in history. Sadly, the current APC governors live in obscene affluence, building new government houses, buying exotic cars, travelling by private jet and displaying an opulence that offends the sensibilities of the very citizens whose commonwealth they were entrusted to steward.

“We commit that our compact stands in direct opposition to this record and that our conduct in office will be measured against it.”

Malami emphasised that the removal of fuel subsidy by the APC-led Federal Government has pushed the masses of our zone into abject poverty.

He said households that had hitherto lived on the fringe of hardship now live in abject poverty, and the supposed gains claimed for the removal of subsidy have brought no positive impact to their daily lives.

Malami noted: “We, the ADC governorship candidates of the seven North-west states, hereby declare our total support for the promise made by the ADC presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, to restore the subsidy as one of the immediate steps to halt the further slide of our people into abject poverty.

“We commit that we will implement a minimum wage of N110,000 for workers across all seven states of the North-west when elected.

“We will not surrender the constitutional authority of our individual states, nor dissolve the distinct priorities of Jigawa, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kebbi, Sokoto and Zamfara.

“Each of us will remain answerable for our own budgets, procurement, civil service, state education and health systems, land administration, internally generated revenue, state agriculture and infrastructure within our borders.”

Malami, however, said that where the people’s problems cross their borders, they commit to govern together to resolve them.

“We will coordinate our security architecture. We will hold ourselves to common standards. We will pool investment where pooling multiplies impact. We will open cross-border trade, share data, build joint infrastructure and speak with one voice in advocacy for our region,” he said.

The former AGF assured the North-west that a technology-enabled surveillance and rapid-response network would be established in each of the 21 senatorial districts across all the seven states of the region.

He said they would deploy drones region-wide and establish a North-west Regional Security Coordination Centre to combine lawful aerial surveillance, community intelligence, emergency reporting and geospatial data into a single chain: surveillance, early warning, command and control, verification and rapid response by the security agencies constitutionally empowered to act.

Malami noted that they would also declare an emergency on education, secure full UBEC access, integrate Almajiri and Tsangaya children into formal schools, support girls’ school attendance, and build a credible system for teacher recruitment, continuous training and mopping up out-of-school children.

He stressed that they would ensure full access to the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF), revitalize primary health care centres, expand midwives, telemedicine and community health insurance deployment.

Malami stressed that they would also establish one specialist hospital in each senatorial district (21 region wide)

“We will cooperate where cooperation works better. We will preserve the constitutional authority and priorities of our states. We will plan before we promise. We will publish what we deliver. We will protect our citizens through reform. We will manage public resources responsibly. And we will submit our performance to independent public scrutiny,” he stated.

The candidates announced the establishment of a Central Coordination Committee chaired by Hon. Abdussamad Dasuki; a Technical Committee chaired by Maj. Gen. Aminu Bande (rtd.) and co-chaired by Prof. Sadiq Abubakar; and a Media and Strategic Communications Committee co-chaired by Salihu Tanko Yakasai.

Earlier, speaking on behalf of the North-west Governorship Strategy Group, Dasuki said the level of poverty and insecurity in the region had never been witnessed before.

He said the candidates have resolved to work together as a team to address the challenges facing the region.

World.title: 2027: Kwara PDP Guber Candidate, Kawu, Decries Campaign Billboard Removal
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Kwara State for 2027 elections, Mr. Suleiman Bolakale Kawu, has condemned the reported removal of his campaign billboards across major streets of Ilorin and other parts of the state, despite the payment of all the required dues to the agency responsible for its operations in the state.

Workers of the Kwara State Signage and  Agency (KWASAA) had reportedly removed Kawu’s campaign billboards mounted at the Geri Alimi Underpass bridge, Agaka and Adabata Junction in Ilorin.

The development, according to THISDAY checks, have continued to cause dissatisfaction within the supporters and leaders of PDP in the state in the past few days.

A statement in Ilorin by the PDP governorship candidate, Kawu, described the development as a disturbing display of intolerance towards legitimate political competition.

Kawu said that if the actions were politically motivated, they would amount to an abuse of administrative power and an attempt to suppress opposing voices.

Kawu maintained that removing his name from billboards would neither diminish his commitment to Kwara nor erase his aspiration to serve the people.

“My name may be removed from a billboard, but my commitment to Kwara cannot be removed, nor can my aspiration to serve or the people’s right to choose their leaders,” he said.

He stressed that Kwara belongs to all its citizens and should remain a place where political competition and divergent views can be expressed freely and peacefully.

Kawu assured the people of Kwara that he would continue to engage them openly and peacefully, regardless of attempts to diminish his political visibility.

“You may remove a billboard, but you cannot remove an idea whose time has come,” he said.

He urged Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq to compete with ideas, programmes and performance rather than attempting to suppress the visibility of political opponents.

The PDP in the state has also condemned KWASAA’s action.

A statement issued in Ilorin Wednesday by the party’s state Publicity Secretary, Hon. Olusegun Olusola Adewara, said: “The people have moved beyond billboards.

“They have made their choices, formed their opinions and developed their political conviction based on their experiences.

“The growing acceptance of PDP, the rising profile of our gubernatorial candidate, Engr. Suleiman BolaKale Kawu Agaka, and the enduring goodwill enjoyed by our leader, H.E. Dr. Abubakar Bukola Saraki, are realities that no governor’s frustration can erase.

“The voices of the people of Kwara cannot be dismantled. Their political choices cannot be pulled down. Their support cannot be removed with government trucks and ladders.”

The PDP therefore called on the KWASAA to immediately stop the removal of the billboards of opposition candidates so as to ensure peace and harmony in the state.

World.title: Nigeria Condemns Fresh Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The Federal Government has condemned the latest attacks by Houthi forces in Yemen on Saudi Arabia, warning that the renewed hostilities pose a grave threat to regional stability and could further endanger civilians and disrupt global energy supplies.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in a statement by its spokesperson, Oluwafemi Adeniyi, said the attacks, which occurred on Monday, September 7, 2026, injured scores of civilians and damaged civil infrastructure in the Kingdom.

Nigeria described the development as a serious threat to the security and sovereignty of Saudi Arabia, as well as a potential source of wider instability across the Middle East.

The government urged all parties involved in the conflict to respect international law and exercise maximum restraint, stressing that further military actions could worsen the situation and place more civilian lives at risk.

Nigeria also warned against actions capable of disrupting the flow of global energy supplies, highlighting the wider economic consequences the prolonged instability in the Middle East could have on countries dependent on the region for energy.

The latest attacks come against the backdrop of the protracted conflict in Yemen involving the Iran-aligned Houthi movement and forces supporting Yemen’s internationally recognised government.

The Houthis, formally known as Ansar Allah, seized control of Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, in 2014, triggering a wider conflict that drew in Saudi Arabia and a coalition of Arab states. Saudi Arabia subsequently led a military intervention in Yemen in 2015 in support of the Yemeni government.

The conflict has since developed into one of the Middle East’s most complex security crises, with repeated missile and drone attacks by the Houthis targeting Saudi territory at various points during the conflict.

Although Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have pursued dialogue and de-escalation efforts in recent years, tensions in and around Yemen have remained closely linked to broader regional conflicts and security developments.

The Houthis have also emerged as a significant actor in regional maritime security, particularly following attacks launched against commercial shipping in the Red Sea amid the wider Middle East crisis. The developments have raised concerns over international trade, shipping routes and energy supplies.

Against this background, Nigeria urged all sides to avoid steps that could trigger further escalation.

The Federal Government said renewed violence could undermine ongoing efforts to promote peace and stability in the region, while exposing more civilians and critical infrastructure to danger.

Nigeria expressed solidarity with the government and people of Saudi Arabia and wished those injured in the attacks a speedy recovery.

The government also reiterated its commitment to supporting peace processes and conciliatory frameworks capable of promoting regional peace, international security and stability.

It stressed that diplomatic efforts remain essential to preventing further escalation and creating conditions for a lasting peace, shared prosperity and development in the Middle East.

World.title: Police Rescue Kidnap Victim, Arrest Suspect in Rivers
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The Rivers State Police Command has rescued a kidnapped woman, Loveth, and arrested a suspected member of the gang allegedly responsible for her abduction in the state.

The police also recovered a vehicle, locally made pistols, ammunition, a mobile phone, identity cards and other exhibits during an intelligence-led operation aimed at tracking the kidnappers.

According to a statement issued Wednesday by the Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Agabe Blessing, Loveth was abducted on September 2, 2026, while seated in front of her shop.

The statement said the assailants, who were armed, fired shots into the air before forcibly taking the victim away in a vehicle.

Following the incident, the Commissioner of Police, Rivers State Command, Olugbenga Adepoju, directed operatives to intensify efforts to identify and apprehend those responsible.

Acting on intelligence, operatives of the Eleme Police Division commenced a coordinated operation to track the suspected kidnappers.

The operation reportedly resulted in an exchange of gunfire between the police and the suspected criminals, during which the victim was successfully rescued.

One of the alleged gang members, identified as 35-year-old Victor Ini, a native of Akwa Ibom State, was arrested.

“In the course of the operation, the police operatives engaged the suspected kidnappers, resulting in an exchange of gunfire. The operatives successfully rescued the kidnapped victim and arrested one member of the gang, one Victor Ini, male, aged 35 years, a native of Akwa Ibom State,” the police said.

“The exhibits recovered included a silver-coloured mini Keke bus with registration number RBC 992 XE, Abuja; two locally made pistols; one live ammunition; one mobile phone; two identity cards; two black gowns; and a vehicle number plate bearing registration number KRK 528 HG.”

The police command said it had intensified intelligence gathering and surveillance operations to identify and apprehend other members of the suspected kidnapping gang.

Adepoju reassured residents that the command remained committed to protecting lives and property and ensuring that criminal elements were brought to justice.

He warned criminals operating in the state that there would be no safe haven for them, stressing that the police would continue to deploy all lawful and available resources to combat kidnapping and other violent crimes.

The commissioner also urged residents to heighten their security consciousness, particularly during the ember months when criminal activities are often expected to increase.

He called on members of the public to remain vigilant and provide the police with credible and timely information that could assist ongoing efforts to combat crime in the state.

World.title: SHOCKING: SAPS K9 Sky dies despite several welfare warnings
World.content:
SAPS K9 Sky receiving treatment after suffering severe injuries. She was later euthanised after police said her injuries became unbearable. Image: Facebook/Ian Cameron

SAPS K9 Sky has died after suffering severe injuries, while fresh allegations suggest police ignored earlier warnings about her welfare.

The South African Police Service (SAPS) confirmed K9 Sky’s death on Wednesday, 9 September. Veterinarians euthanised the former arson-detection dog after her condition deteriorated and her injuries made surgery and anaesthesia extremely dangerous.

Parliament’s Portfolio Committee on Police chairperson Ian Cameron says SAPS’s own veterinary records show officials knew Sky faced serious risks in a kennel environment before the incident that led to her death.



Cameron has opened a criminal case and referred the matter to the NSPCA’s Special Projects Unit and the South African Veterinary Council.

He has also questioned SAPS’s account of the events leading up to Sky’s injuries.

Sky’s condition deteriorated

Cameron said Sky’s condition deteriorated severely before veterinarians made the decision to euthanise her.



She suffered an open fracture to her left front leg, while tissue in the limb had started dying. Her right front leg was also fractured and the skin had begun to die.

According to Cameron, extensive muscle damage caused Sky’s muscles to begin breaking down and turned her urine red.

Doctors also suspected that her organs had started failing.



After consulting Sky’s treating veterinarians, they decided to euthanise her to prevent further suffering.

Onderstepoort will conduct a clinician-led post-mortem examination and compile a formal report on its findings.

Cameron wants investigators to include that report in all probes into Sky’s death.



SAPS records reveal previous concerns

Cameron says a SAPS veterinary certificate signed on 28 August raises serious questions about what police management knew before Sky suffered her fatal injuries.

The certificate records that SAPS admitted Sky to its Roodeplaat veterinary facility in March after she suffered injuries linked to kennel stress and previous escape attempts.

Those injuries included wounds to her face and legs as well as damage to her teeth.



The veterinary record described Sky’s attempts to escape as “persistent and compulsive” and recorded that she continued trying to escape when officials left her unattended.

Veterinarians diagnosed Sky with separation anxiety and severe kennel stress.

According to Cameron, they treated her with Fluoxetine, Gabapentin and Trazodone.



Crucially, he says the certificate recorded that Sky faced a poor prognosis in the SAPS environment and could not remain there without compromising her welfare.

Veterinary staff recorded that assessment just 10 days before the incident that ultimately led to her death.

Questions over plans to rehome Sky

SAPS previously said Sky was no longer an operational K9 and had a history of escaping from kennels at her former K9 base in Limpopo.



Police moved her to the Roodeplaat veterinary facility while officials arranged to place her with a suitable new owner.

SAPS said the donation process remained under way when Sky suffered her injuries.

Cameron, however, says that explanation raises further questions.



According to information supplied to him, SAPS members asked during August for permission to place Sky temporarily in a suitable home while officials completed the formal process.

Cameron says a suitable and willing person had already been identified.

He alleges officials failed to escalate the request that could have removed Sky from the kennel environment.



Cameron now wants SAPS to explain why the placement process took about 160 days despite veterinary personnel knowing that confinement posed a risk to Sky.

He also wants investigators to establish when the process started, what steps officials took and who carried responsibility for each stage.

Cameron calls for accountability

Cameron welcomed Acting National Commissioner Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane’s decision to appoint a senior officer to investigate the circumstances surrounding Sky’s injuries.



However, he said the information initially supplied to Dimpane by the Roodeplaat facility and responsible management could prove incomplete or materially misleading.

Cameron has called for investigators to preserve Sky’s veterinary records, post-mortem findings, biological samples, CCTV footage, kennel registers, duty rosters, inspection records and internal communications.

He also wants independent investigators to examine the conditions at the facility, Sky’s supervision and the conduct of those responsible for her care.



Cameron said SAPS could not rely solely on an internal investigation into its own conduct.

He accused the police service of failing Sky and described its statement mourning the K9 as “deeply hypocritical”.

“Sympathy is no substitute for accountability,” Cameron said.



He added that Sky’s death raised wider questions about how SAPS manages and protects animals entrusted to its care.

“Sky served the police and depended entirely on SAPS for her protection,” Cameron said.

SAPS was contacted for comment, but The South African had not received a response at the time of publication.

World.title: Cape Town’s rainbow crossing vandalised twice within days
World.content:
Cape Town's rainbow crossing was vandalised twice within days, prompting a city restoration pledge: Image Cllr Ian McMahon

Cape Town’s rainbow crossing in the De Waterkant and Green Point area has been vandalised twice within a matter of days.

The city has promised a full restoration of the LGBTQ+ landmark.

The crossing was first damaged over the weekend of 6-7 September. After the city painted it pink as a temporary fix, it was vandalised a second time with religious graffiti reading “Perversion, Romans 1:24-27” and “Jesus is Lord.”



how the story unfolded

Ward 115 Councillor Ian McMahon confirmed the first incident.

He said the crossing sustained significant damage to its rainbow surface over the weekend.

The specialised paint colours needed to fully restore the design weren’t in stock, with a lead time of roughly three months.



Rather than leave the crossing damaged, the city opted to paint it solid pink as an interim solution.

Shortly afterwards, the now-pink crossing was vandalised a second time, with the religious graffiti scrawled across its surface.

According to MambaOnline, police arrested a man in connection with this second incident.



Officials, though, haven’t yet confirmed further details, and it remains unclear whether the same person was responsible for both incidents.

the crossing’s history of controversy

Cape Town installed the rainbow crossing back in 2022 on Somerset Road. The area has long been associated with the city’s LGBTQ+ community, nightlife and venues.

At the time, Mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis said the crossing aimed to send a clear message.



He wanted everyone to feel welcome in a city that embraces diversity.

Opposition followed almost immediately.

For instance, the ACDP’s Marvin Christians argued at the time that the coloured markings violated National Road Traffic Regulations.



These regulations require crossing paint to be white only.

The city responded that the paint used complied with South African National Standards for road markings.

In response to this latest vandalism, the city reaffirmed its commitment to restoring the crossing.



Once the correct paint colours arrive, the city plans to bring back the original design. Officials say, moreover, that vandalism won’t discourage that effort.

It’s a strange thing to watch a single pedestrian crossing become such a lightning rod, twice damaged, twice repainted, and still very much at the centre of a much bigger conversation about who gets to feel welcome in a shared public space.
