* Price sources: Mexico prices were collected from the websites and apps of Walmart México, Costco México, AutoZone México, Telmex, Cinépolis, Petco México, McDonald’s, Starbucks, Netflix, Spotify and Microsoft. Dallas prices were collected from their U.S. equivalents. The Banxico FIX rate of 16.98 published on Sept. 2, 2026, was used as the official exchange rate reference.

World.title: New 11-tower hotel and apartment complex proposed for Bahía de Banderas
World.content:
A major new 11-tower housing and hotel development in Bahía de Banderas, Nayarit, has been proposed at a projected cost of 515 million pesos (US $30.5 million).

The proposal from BM/5096 Business Trust was published in the Environment Ministry’s Ecological Gazette on Aug. 20 for review, and the start of construction is contingent upon the development obtaining the necessary Environmental Impact Assessment (MIA).

The project, known as Ocean II, will cover 65,453 square meters of land, including private land, land reclaimed from the sea and a portion of the Federal Maritime-Terrestrial Zone. It is expected to consist of a hotel zone and a residential zone, accessible from Paseo de los Cocoteros Avenue.

A 187-room hotel will occupy the Palapar Lot within the Los Flamingos Master Condominium across five towers, ranging from five to 10 stories high, while six residential towers will contain 275 apartments. There are plans for basement parking for 784 vehicles.

Planned amenities include restaurants, a spa, a gym, a beach club, an event hall, retail spaces, swimming pools and over 25,000 square meters of green space.

The developers noted in their submission to the Environment Ministry that they expect the project to take around seven years to complete, with the first phase of construction slated to begin in March 2027 and completion expected in 2033.

The announcement is for a general area where beachside development has been controversial, as it is a nesting habitat for the olive ridley sea turtle.

In July, the Environment Ministry revoked a federal concession for a luxury development in Punta de Mita after finding unauthorized construction and environmental violations by developer Cantiles de Mita.

President Sheinbaum visited Nayarit over the weekend to deliver her second annual report, announcing the creation of a Master Plan to conserve beaches, guarantee free access and protect the entire state coastline’s biodiversity.

“I want to tell you that we’ve been working with the [state] governor for over a year on a master plan for tourism in Nayarit, because we don’t want the mangroves destroyed or all the beaches privatized,” said Sheinbaum in a speech.

With reports from El Sol de México and Tribuna de la Bahía

World.title: Mexico fails the 2025 PISA evaluation: A perspective from our CEO
World.content:
Just this morning, the 2025 PISA 2025 results were released and as feared, they are very concerning both on a global scale and for Mexico specifically.

As a reminder, PISA assessments test 760,000 15-year-old students in 91 countries in science, mathematics and reading. The results show a continued decline globally in all three areas with reading being the largest long-term weakness. Singapore students scored highest, followed closely by China, Japan and South Korea.

Mexico, which historically has done poorly, did even worse than in previous years. Some of the lowlights of Mexico’s performance:

Mexico performed below the OECD average in every 2025 PISA domain and placed 64th out of 91 participating countries/economies globally.

The last time the testing was done, in 2022, Mexico placed 51st out of 81 participating countries/economies.

Mexico declined in country rankings in math and reading, as well as compared to its previous performance.

Mexico ranks significantly below the OECD mean in math, science and reading.

This was Mexico’s fifth consecutive decline in reading since 2009. (The test is taken every 3 years.)

Half of Mexican 15-year-olds read below the minimum proficiency threshold. This is the threshold that one needs to be able to read in order to learn.

Other than the slight gain in science, the results are a disaster. Not only is Mexico getting worse in math and reading scores, but actually getting relatively much worse than other countries.

I often write about the potential of the Mexican economy, but these testing results are a significant red flag. I have written before about two concerns regarding the Mexican workforce:

1. The education barrier means companies have to make significant investments in workforce development and training to prepare workers. This is both a financial cost and a time loss, and puts Mexican operations at a disadvantage versus other countries.

2. The strengthening peso increases the cost of the Mexican workforce. A relatively lower-skilled, relatively expensive workforce means that many companies will instead invest in automation and robotics versus investing in workers.

World.title: Goods from Mexico now make up almost one-fifth of the US import market
World.content:
Listen to this article

Mexico captured almost one-fifth of the U.S. import market in July, well ahead of second-placed Canada, shipping a record US $60.55 billion worth of goods to its northern neighbor, according to official U.S. data.

Mexico’s share of the $332.92 billion U.S. import market in July was 18.2%, ahead of Canada (10.1%); China (8.1%); Vietnam (7.9%); and Taiwan (7.7%), according to data published last Thursday by the U.S. Census Bureau and the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis.

In other words, nearly one in every five dollars the United States spent on imports in July was spent on products from Mexico.

Compared to a year earlier, Mexico’s share of the U.S. import market increased 2.7 percentage points in July.

The difference between Mexico and Canada’s shares of the U.S. import market in July 2025 was 4.5 percentage points. In July of this year, the difference was 8.1 points. Similarly, the difference between Mexico and China’s shares of the U.S. import market increased significantly, rising to 10.1 points in July from 6.5 points in the same month of last year.

The increase in Mexico’s share of the U.S. import market coincides with a boom in Mexican exports. The boom is largely driven by a sharp increase in the export of computer equipment, including AI servers, and other electronics to the U.S.

While such products are helping to boost Mexico’s overall export revenue and share of the U.S. import market, their Mexican content is generally very low. That means that a significant share of the revenue Mexico receives from the export of tech products has already been spent on imported inputs, especially from Taiwan.

Mexico’s export revenue increased 33% annually in July

In July — for the first time in any month on record — Mexico’s revenue from selling goods to the United States exceeded $60 billion.

The year-over-year increase in revenue was 33.6% in July. The month-over-month increase was 9.6%.

Canada’s revenue from exports to the United States also increased on an annual basis in July, but only by 4%. Canada’s income declined on a month-over-month basis in July, falling 10%. Canada’s revenue from products shipped to the United States in July was $33.49 billion, equivalent to 55.3% of Mexico’s income in the same month.

China’s revenue from goods shipped to the United States in July was $27.07 billion, up 2.6% from the same month of last year.

Mexico’s exports to the United States reached a record level in July at a time when there was significant uncertainty in the bilateral trade relationship. On July 1, the U.S. government announced that it had declined to renew the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA), the free trade pact that superseded NAFTA in 2020.

Despite that decision, the USMCA remains in effect, allowing most Mexican goods to enter the United States tariff-free and giving Mexico a significant comparative advantage over most of its competitors.

Mexico’s exports to the US increased 16% between January and July

The U.S. data also shows that the United States imported goods from Mexico worth $358.7 billion in the first seven months of 2026. That figure represents an increase of 16% compared to the same period of 2025.

Mexico’s share of the $2.08 trillion U.S. import market between January and July was 17.3%, up from 15% in the same period of last year.

Canada’s share of the U.S. import market remained virtually the same on a year-over-year basis, while China’s share fell almost two percentage points.

Canada’s income from goods shipped to the United States between January and July increased 1.8% to $233.66 billion. Its share of the U.S. import market was 11.24% in the first seven months of the year, an increase of just 0.08 percentage points compared to the same period of last year. Canada and the United States are currently engaged in a significant trade dispute.

China’s revenue from goods shipped to the United States between January and July was $156.39 billion, a 19.4% decrease compared to the same period of last year. Its share of the U.S. import market was 7.5%, down from 9.4% in the same period of last year. China and the United States are engaged in a long-running trade war.

Mexico is the top market for US exports

The U.S. data shows that the United States exported goods worth $34.24 billion to Mexico in July, an increase of 18.3% compared to the same month of 2025. In the first seven months of 2026, the United States’ revenue from goods exported to Mexico was $229.81 billion, a 16.8% year-over-year increase.

In July, and in the first seven months of 2026, Mexico was the top market for U.S. exports. In the first seven months of last year, Canada was the top foreign market for U.S. goods, just ahead of Mexico.

In the first seven months of 2026, U.S. exports generated total revenue of $1.43 trillion. Sixteen per cent of that revenue — or around one in every six dollars — was derived from goods sent to Mexico. After Mexico, the largest markets for U.S. exports between January and July were, in order, Canada, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and China.

Mexico’s trade surplus with US nears $130 billion

Mexico recorded a trade surplus of $26.31 billion with the United States in July. At the end of July, Mexico’s calendar trade surplus with the U.S. was $128.89 billion. At the end of July last year, it was $112.57 billion, 12.7% lower.

The only country that recorded a larger trade surplus with the United States than Mexico in the year to the end of July was Vietnam. The southeast Asian nation sent exports worth $149.61 billion to the United States in the first seven months of the year, while its outlay on imports from the U.S. was $10.75 billion. Vietnam thus recorded a trade surplus of $138.86 billion with the U.S. in the first seven months of the year.

Mexico’s large trade surplus with the United States has angered U.S. President Donald Trump, who takes the view that the U.S. is “losing money” if its imports from a certain country exceed its exports to the same country. On Friday, he threatened in a social media post to “STOP TRADING WITH COUNTRIES WITH WHICH WE HAVE A DEFICIT” if the U.S. Federal Reserve doesn’t lower its benchmark interest rate, which is currently set at 3.50%-3.75%.

Later on Friday, Trump asserted that Mexico has “nothing” the United States needs, apart from “hot tamales” and “tomatoes,” a claim that collides with the reality that the U.S. and Mexican economies are highly integrated and that Mexico ships huge quantities of goods to its northern neighbor on a daily basis. The data on Mexico’s exports to the U.S. in July and in the first seven months of the year — and that on the United States’ exports to Mexico in the same periods — provide clear evidence of that economic interdependence.

World.title: 500 Chihuahua farmers are benefitting from a 20-year-old Tec student’s prize-winning filtration invention
World.content:
A 20-year-old engineering student from a farming family in Chihuahua has won a national award by developing an irrigation filter that could make water go further for drought-stricken farmers.

Luis Ángel Robles Morales, a mechatronics student at Tecnológico de Monterrey’s Chihuahua campus, leads OAKs Filtration, which last week received the 2026 Eugenio Garza Sada Award in the category of student social innovation.

The award — which includes a prize of 1 million pesos (US $59,121) for Robles — was one of three presented Sept. 2 by Tec de Monterrey and FEMSA, the Monterrey-based company that operates OXXO stores and controls Coca-Cola bottling operations in Mexico.

The two entities jointly established the award in 1993 in honor of the late Garza Sada, an industrialist who was among the university’s founders in 1943 and who helped lead a Monterrey business group that later became FEMSA.

Robles’ irrigation filter makes water use more efficient by preventing clogs that lead to wasted water, disrupted harvests and increased maintenance costs.

A persistent problem in drip and sprinkler systems is sand, mud and other particles clogging emitters.

So far, the system has benefited more than 500 farmers in the south-central region of Chihuahua, according to Tec de Monterrey.

Robles comes from a farming family: His grandfather grew corn, chiles and alfalfa, and his father branched off into making filters for irrigation systems.

In Chihuahua, the need for improved irrigation is acute.

From January through August this year, the state received 247.6 millimeters of rain — roughly 9.8 inches and 11.7% less than the same period last year, the newspaper El Diario de Chihuahua reported. By Aug. 15, drought was affecting 28.3% of the state, up from 11.2% in early May.

OAKs Filtration uses a carbon-steel outer casing and a PVC internal filtering element. Robles said the design provides two to three times the filtration area of commercial systems and channels debris toward the filter’s end, allowing it to clean itself through water flow.

In a test described by the digital news platform Expansion ESG, a competing filter clogged after 30 to 60 minutes, while the OAKs filter ran eight uninterrupted hours without pressure loss and was only about one-third full when inspected.

Robles said the price of the OAKs filter system runs from 30,000 to 100,000 pesos (US $1,773 to $5,910), while traditional commercial filters can cost 300,000 to 500,000 pesos (US $17,736 to $29,560).

OAKs was one of three 2026 Garza Sada Award honorees, with a total prize pool of 4.5 million pesos (US $266,000).

The others were pharmaceutical executive and conservationist Eric Hágsater Gartenberg, recognized for humanistic business leadership, and Formando Emprendedores, a nonprofit that provides education and youth-development programs in northern Mexico.

Since its founding in 1993, the award has recognized 81 winners.

Robles said he will devote half of his prize money to the project and half to an international entrepreneurial experience.

With reports from Expansión ESG, EJE Central, El Economista and El Diario de Chihuahua

World.title: Latest PISA survey reveals 4 in 10 Mexican students do not meet basic level in science, math and reading
World.content:
The latest edition of an OECD-conducted global education evaluation reveals a disturbing decline in the skills of Mexican students: four in 10 15-year-olds are scoring below the basic level in science, mathematics and reading.

The test, called the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), has been administered periodically since the turn of the century; this time to 7,843 students from 297 schools in Mexico. The 41.8% of students who scored below the basic level in the science/math/reading triad was more than double the 19.7% average of all countries in the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).

Mexican 15-year-olds as a whole scored 388 points in mathematics, 408 in reading and 414 in science, all well below the OECD averages of 463, 461 and 482, respectively.

Mexican students aren’t just falling behind their global peers — their own results are slipping too. Since the 2022 PISA, Mexico has dropped seven points in both math and reading, even as it held steady in science.

Overall, the current test results are Mexico’s worst since 2009.

While it may be a small consolation to parents and the education community, Mexico is far from the only country experiencing a decline. “Globally, we have seen a dramatic drop, particularly in reading skills,” Andreas Schleicher, the OECD’s Director of Education and Skills, said in an interview with the newspaper El Financiero.

If the first step toward turning things around is a positive attitude, it may already be at hand. The OECD highlighted that 80% of 15-year-old Mexican students stated in the PISA test that they are curious about various topics, up by 7% compared to the global average. Another finding revealed that just 11% of respondents agreed that school is a waste of time, compared to the OECD average of 24%.

In another sense, the poor scores may be a case of Mexico being a victim of its own success. As pointed out in a report cited by Animal Politico, “Given the expansion of secondary education to previously marginalized populations, [Mexico’s] results appear somewhat more positive. ”

Meanwhile, Mexico is struggling, along with the rest of the world, with modern impediments to educational performance. According to Education International, the largest global federation of teachers, the decline in student performance can be attributed “to shorter attention spans, excessive use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the global teacher shortage.”

Despite that, the top-performing countries in all PISA areas were China, Singapore, South Korea, Estonia and Canada.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: Authorities seize 300 computers from cryptomining farm siphoning power from Puebla grid
World.content:
Federal authorities dismantled a clandestine cryptocurrency mining farm in the state of Puebla where approximately 300 computers illegally connected to a hydroelectric complex were found to be mining digital assets.

The cryptomining farm was discovered in Tlaola, a municipality in the remote Sierra Norte region of Puebla, thanks to a joint investigation carried out by the Federal Attorney General’s Office, the Navy and state prosecutors.

En Tlaola, un inmueble presuntamente utilizado para minería de criptomonedas fue asegurado por @FGRMexico, @SEMAR_mx y Seguridad Pública Estatal del @Gob_Puebla. Se localizó infraestructura eléctrica, internet satelital y equipos especializados en generación de activos… pic.twitter.com/lfgKk3pY3s — Secretaría de Seguridad Pública (@SSPGobPue) September 6, 2026

During the operation, authorities uncovered a highly equipped digital operations center. Agents seized large-scale electrical and technological infrastructure that included transformers, medium-voltage terminals, 300 specialized computer units (GPUs) and operational satellite internet antennas.

The initial criminal charge being prepared is energy theft, but prosecutors say money laundering charges have not been ruled out. Forensic accountants are tracing the origin of the funds used to acquire the expensive technological hardware.

State authorities have confirmed that investigators have expanded their search to neighboring municipalities in anticipation of similar operations.

Puebla Security Minister Francisco Sánchez said the “farms” are part of a network that takes advantage of the proximity to hydroelectric facilities in the Sierra Norte to steal massive volumes of energy.

Cryptomining consumes a significant amount of energy and produces a lot of noise, Sánchez said, so remote and isolated locations away from communities are favored.

“We have been monitoring this … area of ​​the state, especially due to its proximity to the [Nuevo Necaxa] dam,” he said, adding that the discovery of a large-scale power line connection helped the authorities locate the clandestine farm.

Last year, officials busted a crypto farm in the small Puebla community near the dam where properties owned by the Electrical Workers Union were allegedly being used to operate mining facilities powered by illegal connections to the Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) power grid.

Two other mining operations straddling the border between Puebla and Tlaxcala were also dismantled in 2025.

Cryptocurrency mining — which is not illegal in Mexico, although cryptocurrencies are not legal tender here — is a process that uses computers to solve complex mathematical operations in order to validate transactions and earn rewards in digital assets.

In its latest report on non-technical losses covering the period from January to July 2024, the CFE estimated that energy theft, meter tampering and illegal connections cost the company approximately 13.8 billion pesos (US $817 million).

Cryptocurrencies are increasingly being used to move funds between financial users and countries quickly, cheaply and discreetly, such that they have become a popular money-laundering tool for criminal groups.

With reports from El País, Xataka México, Debate and La Jornada de Oriente

World.title: Why Azul Keeps Losing in Maceio’s Small-Claims Courts
World.content:
BRAZIL · CONSUMER LAW

Key Facts — The pattern Small-claims courts in Maceio have ruled against Azul repeatedly through 2026 over cancelled and disrupted flights.

— March R$6,000 in moral damages for a couple whose Rio Branco to Maceio journey arrived more than 16 hours late. Judge Sergio Roberto da Silva Carvalho, 6th Special Civil Court of the Capital.

— May R$3,000 plus R$1,306.21 reimbursed, after a Maceio to Recife passenger was put on a bus instead of a plane. Judge Nelson Tenorio, 5th Special Civil Court.

— The defence that fails Unscheduled maintenance. Courts treat it as an internal business risk, not an external event that breaks liability.

— Not a fine These are civil damages paid to individual passengers. There is no confirmed regulator penalty against Azul in 2026.

— The federal backdrop The Supreme Court froze airline delay litigation nationally in November 2025, then clarified in May 2026 that the freeze does not cover cases where the airline itself is at fault.

Brazil’s Supreme Court tried to stop the flood of airline compensation suits. The carve-out it left is exactly the argument that keeps beating Azul in Alagoas.

Why Azul Keeps Losing in Maceio’s Small-Claims Courts

A run of consumer rulings in Alagoas has gone against Azul this year, and they turn on the same point: when an airline cancels a flight for maintenance it did not plan, Brazilian courts do not treat that as bad luck.

What the Courts Awarded

On 17 March a Maceio small-claims judge ordered Azul to pay R$6,000 in moral damages to a couple whose flight from Rio Branco was cancelled without prior notice. They were scheduled to land at 5:00 pm on 27 September 2025 and arrived at 9:05 am the next morning, a gap of more than 16 hours. The judge was Sergio Roberto da Silva Carvalho, sitting in the 6th Special Civil Court of the capital, case 0700898-36.2025.8.02.0075.

On 5 May, published the following day, Judge Nelson Tenorio of the 5th Special Civil Court ordered R$3,000 in moral damages plus R$1,306.21 in reimbursement to a passenger booked from Maceio to Recife. His flight was cancelled and he was rebooked onto ground transport. He reached Recife at about 12:40 pm instead of 10:30 am.

The reasoning in that second case is the sharper one. Substitute road transport, the judge held, does not amount to the service the passenger bought. A bus is not a delayed plane. It is a different product.

A third award, reported in July, put R$2,500 against the airline in an Alagoas baggage case. The Rio Times has not been able to obtain that ruling directly and is reporting the figure at the level of the local press account.

The Argument That Keeps Failing

Azul’s defence in these cases is unscheduled maintenance. Brazilian civil law distinguishes between fortuito externo, an outside event that severs the chain of liability, and fortuito interno, a risk that belongs to the business itself.

Alagoas judges have put aircraft maintenance firmly in the second box. Keeping a fleet airworthy is not an act of God. It is the cost of running an airline, and the passenger did not agree to carry it.

That is not a local eccentricity. The same doctrine has produced awards elsewhere in Brazil, including a R$10,000 judgment against Azul over a 72-hour delay in which the carrier also cited unplanned maintenance.

The maintenance defence is what keeps these cases outside the national freeze.

What Azul does. Azul S.A., together with its subsidiaries, provides air transportation services in Brazil and internationally. It is also involved in the cargo or mail; passenger charter; development of frequent-flyer programs; intellectual property owner; travel packages; funding: aircraft financing; and provision of maintenance and hangarage services for aircraft, engines, parts and pieces, aircraft acquisition,…

Why These Cases Are Still Moving

They should not be, on a quick reading of the docket. On 26 November 2025 Justice Dias Toffoli of the Supreme Federal Court ordered a national suspension of lawsuits over airline liability for delays and cancellations, under Tema 1.417.

The court’s stated concern was volume. Brazil generates roughly one airline lawsuit per 227 passengers. The comparison offered was the United States at one per 1.2 million.

In early May 2026 the Supreme Court clarified the scope of that freeze: it does not reach cases where the failure is the airline’s own. Fortuito interno is outside the suspension.

That clarification is the whole reason the Alagoas rulings kept coming. The maintenance defence is not just losing on the merits. Raising it is what takes the case out of the national pause and puts it back in front of a judge.

What This Is Not

None of this is a regulatory penalty. Damages awarded by a juizado especial go to the passenger who sued. They are indenizacao, not multa.

The Rio Times found no confirmed administrative fine from Brazil’s civil aviation regulator against Azul in 2026. The fines that surfaced in searches were against other parties, including an airport operator and individual disruptive passengers.

The distinction matters for anyone reading these headlines as a compliance signal. A pattern of consumer judgments says something about service reliability and about legal exposure. It does not say the regulator has acted.

Azul left Chapter 11 in February 2026 and moved its listing to NYSE American in May.

The Company Behind the Cases

Azul left United States Chapter 11 protection on 20 February 2026, having completed its restructuring before the bankruptcy court for the Southern District of New York, repaid its debtor-in-possession financing and consolidated its stock.

It moved its listing to NYSE American in late May. The shares fell heavily later in the year after a share issue diluted existing holders.

A carrier rebuilding its balance sheet has an obvious incentive to defer maintenance spending and to defend compensation claims hard. The Alagoas rulings are what happens when both of those meet a consumer code that puts the operational risk on the operator.

More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much has Azul been ordered to pay in Alagoas?

The documented 2026 awards are R$6,000 in March and R$3,000 plus R$1,306.21 in reimbursement in May, both from Maceio small-claims courts. A further R$2,500 baggage award was reported in July.

Are these fines?

No. They are civil damages paid to the individual passengers who sued. There is no confirmed regulatory fine against Azul in 2026.

Why does the maintenance defence fail?

Brazilian courts treat unscheduled maintenance as fortuito interno, a risk internal to the business, which does not break the carrier’s liability to the passenger.

Did the Supreme Court not suspend these cases?

It suspended airline delay litigation nationally in November 2025 under Tema 1.417, then clarified in May 2026 that the suspension does not apply where the airline itself is at fault. Maintenance cases fall outside it.

Is Azul still in bankruptcy?

No. It exited Chapter 11 on 20 February 2026 and later moved its listing to NYSE American.

Sources: Alagoas24Horas, Tribuna Hoje, Folha de Alagoas, O Alagoano, Conjur, STF, InfoMoney.

World.title: Gerdau Wins Its Sector in a Year Profit Fell 69 Percent
World.content:
BRAZIL · COMPANIES

Key Facts — The award Gerdau took the metallurgy and steel category of the 26th Valor 1000 for a fifth consecutive year, awarded 8 September 2026.

— The wording The fifth-year count comes from Gerdau’s own release. Valor’s article does not state a consecutive count.

— The revenue Net revenue of 69.9 billion reais in 2025, up 4.2 percent, ranking 17th overall.

— The profit Net income of 1.418 billion reais, down 69.2 percent, at a net margin of 2.0 percent.

— The pivot Chief executive Gustavo Werneck says investment goes where returns are best, and that today means the United States.

— The word he used Werneck describes operating in Brazil as survival mode.

Gerdau won its sector in a year its net profit fell by more than two thirds. The award is about North America, and its chief executive says so plainly.

Gerdau Wins Its Sector in a Year Profit Fell 69 Percent

Gerdau took the metallurgy and steel category of the 26th Valor 1000 yearbook, awarded on Tuesday 8 September 2026. Its own release describes it as a fifth consecutive win.

The Numbers Behind It

Valor’s own ranking places Gerdau 17th overall, down from 16th, on net revenue of 69.9 billion reais in 2025, up 4.2 percent.

On that same table, earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation fell 30.1 percent to 7.4 billion reais, and net income fell 69.2 percent to 1.418 billion, a net margin of 2.0 percent.

Gerdau’s own release cites adjusted earnings of 10.1 billion reais, net revenue of 69.9 billion and sales of 11.6 million tonnes. The revenue figures agree; the earnings gap is adjusted against unadjusted, and each should carry its source.

One point of care on the count. The fifth consecutive year comes from Gerdau. Valor’s article does not state one, though Gerdau’s own archive is consistent, describing 2025 as the fourth.

Where the Money Is Going

Chief executive Gustavo Werneck was direct about the geography. Investment goes where the prospects are better and the best returns can be had, he said, and today that is the United States.

He expects the company to announce new expansion investments there. The country is reindustrialising and steel demand is growing, he said.

He added that Gerdau never imagined its North American results could be so far ahead of its Brazilian ones.

On Brazil he was blunter. The company has stopped investing to grow there. There is no point expanding and being left with idle capacity.

He said Gerdau compares its production costs and performance indicators against the main international producers and comes out ahead, but that in Brazil it has to fight to keep living in the face of predatory competition. Valor attributes to him the phrase that the company operates in Brazil in survival mode.

Gerdau S.A., together with its subsidiaries, operates as a steel producer company. It operates through Brazil Business, North America Business, and South America Business segments. The company offers rebars, bars, wires, thick plates, hot rolled coils, billets, blooms, plates, wire rods, and structural profiles. It also provides special steel products for agricultural,…

Why the Contrast Exists

Gerdau has been arguing for stronger trade protection for two years. Chinese imports have occupied close to a quarter of the Brazilian market.

Brazil applies tariff quotas on 19 steel product categories, with a 25 percent tariff above quota, renewed for June 2026 to 2027. In January it added a 25 percent import tax on nine codes of pre-painted steel from China and India.

Those measures are working at the margin. Steel product imports fell 17.6 percent in the first half of 2026 to 2.9 million tonnes, and the industry body cut its full-year import forecast to 6.3 million tonnes.

But domestic demand fell too. Apparent consumption dropped 5.3 percent and crude steel output 1.5 percent over the same period.

Gerdau cut its 2026 capital spending to 4.7 billion reais, 21.7 percent below the previous plan. Werneck said last October that without intensified protection the company would debate whether to maintain the volume of resources it applies in the country.

Net revenue rose 4.2 percent to 69.9 billion reais, but on Valor’s table net income fell 69.2 percent to 1.418 billion, a margin of 2.0 percent.

Why the gap in the earnings figures?

Gerdau cites adjusted earnings of 10.1 billion reais; Valor’s ranking shows 7.4 billion unadjusted. Both are as published by their sources.

Where is Gerdau investing?

North America. The chief executive says investment goes where returns are best and expects new United States expansion, while describing Brazilian operations as survival mode.

World.title: Suzano Tops Valor 1000 in Pulp and Paper on Record Volume
World.content:
BRAZIL · COMPANIES

Key Facts — The award Suzano was named champion of the pulp and paper sector in the 26th Valor 1000 yearbook, awarded on 8 September 2026.

— The revenue Net revenue of 50.1 billion reais in 2025, up 5.7 percent, ranking 28th among Brazil’s thousand largest companies.

— The profit Net income of 13.4 billion reais, up 290.7 percent, at a net margin of 26.8 percent.

— The volume Record sales of 14.2 million tonnes.

— The gap Klabin, second in the sector, ranks 69th overall with 20.7 billion reais. Suzano is 2.4 times its size.

— The overall winner Itau Unibanco was named Empresa de Valor 2026.

Suzano finished a 70 billion real investment cycle and posted its best sales volume on record. The half-year that followed was harder.

Suzano Tops Valor 1000 in Pulp and Paper on Record Volume

Suzano was named champion of the pulp and paper sector in the 26th edition of the Valor 1000 yearbook, awarded in Sao Paulo on Tuesday 8 September 2026. It ranks 28th among Brazil’s thousand largest companies.

What the Ranking Measures

Valor 1000 is Brazil’s principal business yearbook, ranking the country’s thousand largest companies across 27 sectors. It is produced by the newspaper Valor Economico with Serasa Experian and the Getulio Vargas Foundation’s Sao Paulo business school, which homologates the criteria.

This edition ranks companies on their 2025 results.

Suzano’s 2025 net revenue was 50.1 billion reais, up 5.7 percent. Net income reached 13.4 billion, up 290.7 percent, at a net margin of 26.8 percent and a return on equity of 35.2 percent.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation came to 21.9 billion reais, down 11.9 percent. Total assets stood at 167.9 billion.

Klabin is second in the sector, 69th overall, at 20.7 billion reais. Itau Unibanco took the overall Empresa de Valor award.

What Drove the Year

Sales reached 14.2 million tonnes, a company record. Suzano exports about 88 percent of its output.

It concluded a five-year investment cycle of some 70 billion reais.

In July it took 51 percent of Arbex, the tissue joint venture with Kimberly-Clark, in a transaction valued at 3.7 billion dollars. That lifts its mill count to 36, of which 14 are its own, twelve in Brazil and two in the United States.

Capacity stands at 13.4 million tonnes of pulp and around 2 million tonnes of paper.

Chief executive Beto Abreu said that in 2026, because the company consolidates all of Arbex’s result, there will be a relevant increase in revenue from the joint venture entering the portfolio.

The Harder Half-Year

The first half of 2026 was weaker. Revenue fell 9 percent to 22.5 billion reais and net profit fell 46 percent to 6.119 billion.

On costs, he said the company has been efficient enough to absorb higher gas and diesel prices and holds derivative instruments that protect it against those increases.

Leverage stands at 3.4 times, against a target of 2.5. Abreu said the strategy is to concentrate all cash generation on reducing it, and that the reduction will come as the investments mature.

World.title: Smart Fit’s Best Business Is the One Without Gyms
World.content:
BRAZIL · COMPANIES

Key Facts — The growth TotalPass reached 2.2 million users across Brazil and Mexico in the second quarter, up 70 percent.

— The revenue Segment revenue of 230 million reais, up 47 percent, with gross profit up 79 percent to 195 million.

— The margin 84.7 percent gross margin, against a group that mostly runs gyms.

— The weight Eleven percent of consolidated revenue but 17 percent of consolidated gross profit.

— The share Thirty-five percent of active monthly users in Brazil, up eight points. Seventy-nine percent market share in Mexico.

— The market reaction Smart Fit shares fell 7.82 percent on results day, the worst in the Ibovespa that session.

Smart Fit’s fastest-growing business does not own a single treadmill. It is also the reason the shares fell.

Smart Fit’s Best Business Is the One Without Gyms

TotalPass, Smart Fit’s corporate wellness platform, reached 2.2 million users in the second quarter, up 70 percent. It now supplies 17 percent of the group’s gross profit.

What TotalPass Is

TotalPass is a corporate benefits platform. Companies buy it for their employees, who then get access to a network of partner gyms rather than only to Smart Fit’s own.

It is the asset-light layer on top of a business that otherwise owns and operates gyms. It competes directly with Wellhub, formerly Gympass.

The partner network covers more than 34,000 gyms in Brazil across 2,000 cities, or about 44,000 establishments including Smart Fit’s own.

It sits inside the group’s Others reporting segment.

The Numbers

Second-quarter segment revenue reached 230 million reais, up 47 percent. Gross profit rose 79 percent to 195 million, at a gross margin of 84.7 percent.

That is 11 percent of consolidated revenue and 17 percent of consolidated gross profit.

Users reached 2.2 million across Brazil and Mexico, up 70 percent. In Brazil the platform holds 35 percent of active monthly users, eight points more than a year earlier. In Mexico it holds 79 percent market share.

Jose Luis Rizzardo, the group’s chief financial officer, said TotalPass is always a pleasant surprise, both in the speed at which things happen and in their magnitude.

A widely circulated report putting TotalPass at 15 percent of gross profit describes the first quarter. The second-quarter figure is 17 percent.

Why the Shares Fell Anyway

Group revenue reached 2.18 billion reais in the quarter, up 22 percent, with earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation up 24 percent to 712 million.

Below that line it was weaker. Reported net profit was 156 million reais, about 30 percent below one bank’s estimate, and cash generation came in at 530 million against 694 million expected. Net debt stood at 4.6 billion reais and leverage at 1.20 times.

The shares fell 7.82 percent to 18.38 reais on 6 August, the largest drop in the Ibovespa that session and the second most traded stock on the exchange.

Morgan Stanley called it a good quarter, messy below the earnings line. Joao Pedro Soares of Citibank said results were mixed but that the bank remains constructive on the growth trajectory.

XP called it a strong positive surprise, with margin expansion beating forecasts in a seasonally weak quarter.

The Group Around It

Smart Fit ended the quarter with 2,170 gyms, up 19 percent, of which 1,746 are company-owned. Mature-unit gross margin was 51 percent.

Guidance is for 330 to 350 new gyms in 2026, with 98 opened by mid-year.

The company attributes revenue growth mainly to a 10 percent increase in the average ticket at company-owned gyms and an 8 percent rise in the average student base.

Edgard Gomes Corona, founder and chairman, has said the sector suffers oversupply, with many entrants extremely leveraged. He calls TotalPass a strategic lever and says Smart Fit pays partner gyms better than rivals do.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is TotalPass?

Smart Fit’s corporate wellness platform. Companies buy it as an employee benefit and staff access a network of partner gyms, not only Smart Fit’s own.

How fast is it growing?

Users reached 2.2 million in the second quarter, up 70 percent, with segment revenue up 47 percent and gross profit up 79 percent.

Why did the shares fall?

Weak cash generation and below-the-line items. Reported net profit came in about 30 percent under one bank’s estimate, and the shares fell 7.82 percent on results day.

Who does it compete with?

Wellhub, formerly Gympass, in the corporate wellness benefits market.

World.title: Brazil’s Electric Record Depends on How You Count It
World.content:
BRAZIL · AUTOS

Key Facts — The record Electrified vehicles took 24.4 percent of Brazilian new-car registrations in August, an all-time high.

— The catch That figure covers all electrified vehicles, including mild hybrids that never run on electricity alone.

— Pure electric Battery electric vehicles were 27,159 registrations, about 42.6 percent of the electrified total and roughly a tenth of the whole market.

— The plug-in number Battery electric plus plug-in hybrid comes to 46,991, or 73.7 percent of the electrified total.

— The growth Electrified registrations more than doubled year on year, from 24,755 in August 2025.

— The leader BYD took 9.30 percent of the total market and third place overall for the first time.

Brazil set an electrified vehicle record in August. Whether it set an electric vehicle record depends entirely on which definition you use.

Electrified vehicles reached 24.4 percent of Brazilian new-car registrations in August 2026, a record. Most of that total is not battery electric.

What the Number Contains

The manufacturers’ association Anfavea puts the August share at 24.4 percent. The consultancy Bright Consulting puts it at 24.3 percent on a total of 63,709 electrified vehicles.

Inside that total, battery electric vehicles were 27,159 units, or 42.6 percent. Plug-in hybrids were 19,832, or 31.1 percent.

Full hybrids were 9,716, or 15.3 percent. Mild hybrids were 6,401, or 10.0 percent, and extended-range vehicles 601.

A mild hybrid never runs on electricity alone. Including it in an electric share is a definitional choice, not a neutral one.

The defensible plug-in number is battery electric plus plug-in hybrid: 46,991 vehicles, 73.7 percent of the electrified total. Pure battery electric is roughly a tenth of the whole market.

The Growth Is Real Either Way

August 2025 saw 24,755 electrified registrations. August 2026 more than doubled that.

Over the first eight months Bright counts 367,500 electrified registrations against 156,700 a year earlier, a rise of 134 percent. Anfavea counts 372,000, up 125.8 percent.

The total market took 275,100 vehicles in August and 1.975 million over eight months, up 18.4 percent.

So electrified vehicles are growing about seven times faster than the market they sit in.

Who Is Selling Them

BYD registered 24,467 vehicles in August, 9.30 percent of the total market and third place overall for the first time. Its year-to-date total of 146,930 already exceeds its full-year 2025 figure of about 112,000.

It holds close to 60 percent of the battery electric segment and has led retail sales for five straight months. Its Dolphin was the top retail model at 5,964 units.

Alexandre Baldy, senior vice president of BYD Brasil, said the evolution presented itself two years ahead of the company’s own planning.

GWM is close behind on growth, up 99.7 percent over eight months against BYD’s 118.6 percent. Its Haval H6 took 6,433 registrations in August, tenth overall.

GWM plays both hybrid formats. In May the Haval H6 plug-in outsold the BYD Song Pro, 4,037 to 3,565.

The Tariff Clock

Brazil’s foreign trade chamber has been raising import duties on electric vehicles in stages.

Semi-knocked-down kits went to 35 percent from 1 July 2026 and are at that level now. Completely-knocked-down kits sit at 14 percent to 31 December 2026, then rise to 35 percent from 1 January 2027.

A zero-tariff quota was renewed for six months from 1 July 2026, covering 463 million dollars of imports.

Anfavea opposed the quota, describing it as a great concern for domestic manufacturers and parts suppliers.

More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What share did electric vehicles take in August?

Electrified vehicles took 24.4 percent, a record. Battery electric alone was about a tenth of the market, at 27,159 registrations.

What counts as electrified?

Battery electric, plug-in hybrid, full hybrid, mild hybrid and extended-range vehicles. Mild hybrids, 10 percent of the total, never run on electricity alone.

Who is leading?

BYD, with 24,467 registrations in August, 9.30 percent of the total market and third place overall for the first time.

What happens to import tariffs?

Semi-knocked-down kits are already at 35 percent. Completely-knocked-down kits rise from 14 to 35 percent on 1 January 2027.

Sources: Anfavea via eixos, Bright Consulting via AutoIndustria, MoveNews, Despachante DOK, Agencia Brasil.

World.title: Brazil Puts a Battery Inside a Transmission Auction
World.content:
BRAZIL · ENERGY

Key Facts — The consultation Brazil’s electricity regulator opens public consultation 032 of 2026 on 10 September. Contributions close on 26 October.

— The auction 30 April 2027, covering 12 lots across 13 states in all five regions.

— The scale 3,245 kilometres of new transmission line and 1,386 MVA of transformation capacity, at an estimated 12.9 billion reais.

— The first Lot 5 is the first battery storage system contracted at transmission level in Brazil’s national grid.

— The battery 100 MW and 200 MWh, at Cruzeiro do Sul and Feijo in Acre, for supply reliability in the isolated west of the state.

— The term Eleven lots run 30 years. The battery lot runs 18, matched to battery service life.

Brazil is about to auction a battery as part of a transmission concession for the first time. It is going to Acre, not to the wind farms of the northeast.

Brazil Puts a Battery Inside a Transmission Auction

Brazil’s electricity regulator approved on 8 September the terms of a transmission auction that for the first time contracts a battery storage system as part of a concession. Public consultation opens on 10 September.

What Is Being Auctioned

The auction is set for 30 April 2027. It covers 12 lots spread across 13 states in all five regions of the country.

Together they cover 3,245 kilometres of new transmission line and 1,386 MVA of transformation capacity, at an estimated investment of 12.9 billion reais.

Construction windows run from 36 to 60 months after contract signature.

Eleven lots carry 30-year concessions. The consultation, number 032 of 2026, opens on 10 September and closes for contributions on 26 October.

The Battery Lot

Lot 5 is the first battery storage system to be contracted at transmission level in Brazil’s interconnected system.

It is specified at 100 MW and 200 MWh, at Cruzeiro do Sul and Feijo in Acre. The stated purpose is supply reliability for the isolated west of that state.

The concession runs 18 years rather than 30, matched to the service life of the batteries. Grid-forming inverter requirements are specified.

Agnes Costa, the reporting director at the regulator, said the future transmission company must address investment and the maintenance of system availability throughout the contract term.

The concept was flagged by director-general Sandoval Feitosa in August 2025, as the possibility of auctioning storage systems as an integral part of transmission concessions.

One Link Worth Not Making

Brazil does have a serious curtailment problem, and it is concentrated in the northeast. In the first quarter of 2026 an average 2,843 MW was cut, 17.2 percent of potential generation, against 2,436 MW a year earlier.

Across 2025, 20.6 percent of available solar and wind output was lost. The northeast alone accounted for an average 2,233 MW between January and April, against 476 MW in the southeast.

Lot 5 is not the answer to that. It sits in Acre, in the north, and its purpose is local reliability.

The curtailment answer is a different auction. Brazil’s first dedicated battery auction is scheduled for 2 and 4 December 2026, with 6,091 distinct projects registered and the northeast accounting for 71.1 percent of registered capacity.

The market expects up to 6 gigawatts to be contracted there, against a 2 gigawatt minimum.

More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is being auctioned?

Twelve transmission lots across 13 states, covering 3,245 kilometres of line and 1,386 MVA of transformation, at an estimated 12.9 billion reais. The auction is on 30 April 2027.

What is new about it?

Lot 5 contracts a 100 MW, 200 MWh battery system as part of a transmission concession, the first time Brazil has done this in its national grid.

Where is the battery going?

Cruzeiro do Sul and Feijo in Acre, for supply reliability in the isolated west of the state. It is not aimed at northeastern curtailment.

When can the public comment?

Consultation 032 of 2026 opens on 10 September 2026 and closes for contributions on 26 October.

Sources: O Setor Eletrico, Poder360, eixos, Petronoticias, Canal Solar, Agencia Gov.

World.title: Foreign Money Returns to B3 After a Heavy August
World.content:
BRAZIL · MARKETS

Key Facts — The figure Foreign investors put a net 1.390 billion reais into B3-listed equities in the session of 2 September.

— The lag That number was published on 4 September. B3 reports foreign flow on a two-day delay.

— The month The first three sessions of September brought a net 3.9 billion reais, including 1.7 billion on 3 September alone.

— The year Year-to-date figures range from 20.5 to 22.9 billion reais depending on the series used.

— The reversal August saw a net outflow of 18.1 billion reais.

— The index The Ibovespa closed at 187,366.84 on 8 September, up 1.2 percent and its highest since 4 May.

Foreign money came back to Brazil in the first week of September. What it is buying tells you what it thinks is coming.

Foreign Money Returns to B3 After a Heavy August

One-stop reference Company Intelligence Every listed company in Latin America — financials, ownership and structure for 1,450+ companies across 26 exchanges, in one place. Browse the directory →

Foreign investors bought a net 1.390 billion reais of B3-listed equities in the trading session of 2 September. The figure was published two days later, on B3’s standard reporting lag.

Read the Date Carefully

B3 publishes foreign investor flow with a two-day delay. A number released on 4 September describes the session of 2 September.

That distinction matters when the flow is being used as a signal, because it is always describing a market that has already moved.

The month-to-date total through 2 September was 2.201 billion reais.

B3 also changed the way it delivers information on index futures balances, and that data was temporarily unavailable on its website.

The Wider Flow

The first three sessions of September brought a net 3.9 billion reais, of which 1.7 billion came on 3 September alone.

That follows an August net outflow of 18.1 billion reais, with the monthly deficit peaking at 23.2 billion on 20 August.

Year-to-date figures differ by series. One puts the 2026 total at 20.491 billion reais through 2 September, another at 22.2 billion through 3 September, and a third at 22.9 billion through 31 August. They are not reconcilable from public sources, so each should carry its own attribution.

Over the same opening days institutional investors sold a net 1.6 billion reais and retail investors 2 billion.

Bank of America calculated roughly 6 billion reais of equity inflows over a ten-day window, partially reversing about 20 billion of outflows over the prior three months. It upgraded Brazilian equities to overweight and projected the policy rate at 11.25 percent by the end of 2027.

What They Are Buying, and Why

Marco Saravalle, chief strategist at Krivo Capital, said it is not only the election trade; oil is helping too.

Rafael Perretti, economist and analyst at Clear, said that when foreign money comes in, it goes into the most liquid shares. Mining, oil and banking receive allocations first.

The Ibovespa closed at 187,366.84 points on 8 September, up 1.2 percent and its highest since 4 May. It is up about 6 percent in September and 16.81 percent this year.

What is the year-to-date figure?

Where is the money going?

Into the most liquid shares first, according to Clear’s Rafael Perretti, meaning mining, oil and banking.

World.title: WEG Builds for Europe From Turkey, in Two Separate Projects
World.content:
BRAZIL · COMPANIES

Key Facts — Two projects WEG has a 28 million euro gearbox plant under construction in Manisa and a motor line running in Izmir. They are not the same thing.

— The factory Announced in December 2024, 12,000 square metres, 150 jobs, due to start operating in 2027.

— The motors A new aluminium motor line at the former Volt Electric Motor plant in Izmir, serving European customers.

— The speed WEG says it delivers to European customers in seven to ten days, with production lead times of four to six weeks.

— The scale About 2,000 motors a day in Izmir, an annual capacity near one million units.

— The acquisition WEG bought Volt Electric Motor in September 2024 for 88 million dollars.

A motor maker from Santa Catarina is now building for Europe from Turkey. The reason is distance, not cost.

WEG Builds for Europe From Turkey, in Two Separate Projects
