Congress looks to restart Punjab outreach

The Congress is now looking to revive its organisational and electoral activities in Punjab ahead of the 2027 polls.

The party is planning a statewide yatra in Punjab featuring Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, which could be held towards the end of September or in early October, subject to the festival calendar.

The party had announced its election-related committees on July 1, but their functioning was affected by the subsequent differences within the state unit.

With Pilot replacing Baghel as the Punjab in-charge, Congress leaders have publicly welcomed the change as the party prepares for the next Assembly election.

World.title: Baba Neem Karoli’s granddaughters claim their ancestral home illegally occupied by trust
World.content:
Neem Karoli dham

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A dispute has erupted over the ancestral home of Hindu saint Baba Neem Karoli Maharaj in Uttar Pradesh, with his six granddaughters alleging that the property is being illegally occupied and controlled by a trust headed by their aunt, PTI reported.Following the complaint, Firozabad District Magistrate Santosh Kumar Sharma has constituted a three-member committee to investigate the ownership and management of the property, according to PTI.The committee is headed by additional district magistrate (Judicial) Arvind Kumar Dwivedi and includes Tundla Sub-Divisional Magistrate Divya Singh and District Tourism Officer Vishal Srivastava.The dispute concerns house number 154 and adjoining structures in Akbarpur village under Tundla tehsil, the birthplace of Baba Neem Karoli, whose original name was Lakshmi Narayan Sharma, according to PTI.The property, which is being developed as a tourist attraction by the Uttar Pradesh tourism department, includes the saint's meditation room, dining area, guest quarters and bedroom.The ancestral residence is a duplex built on a plot measuring around 4,000 square feet and is currently managed by the Shri Neem Karoli Maharaj Trust, headed by the saint's daughter Girija Devi Bhatele. His late wife Rambeti was its former president.According to family sources cited by PTI, the dispute came to the fore during a family event on August 24, when the six daughters of the saint's late son Dharm Narayan Sharma were allegedly denied accommodation in rooms at the ancestral property.Following the incident, the six granddaughters, Sunita Sharma, Archana Sharma, Vandana Sharma, Bhavna Rawat, Ritu Tiwari and Richa Rawat, submitted a representation to the District Magistrate seeking that the ancestral residence be freed from the Trust's control, PTI reported.Manoj Rawat, husband of Bhavna Rawat, confirmed to PTI that relevant property documents had been submitted to the inquiry committee after it sought them.However, Dhananjay Sharma, son of the saint's other late son Anek Singh Sharma, rejected the allegations and said that the property had been handed over to the Trust in accordance with Baba Neem Karoli's wishes.He expressed concern over the public nature of the dispute and appealed to family members to resolve the matter amicably.Trust secretary Sanjay Gupta also denied allegations of illegal occupation and rejected claims of an internal dispute within the Trust. He said he had been appointed by Dharm Narayan Sharma and continued to serve the institution.Gupta told PTI that the Trust had not received any official notice from the district administration so far.The dispute comes amid renewed public interest in Baba Neem Karoli's life and legacy following the release of Hanuman Ansh, a devotional biographical film based on the saint's life.Released on August 7, 2026, the low-budget film starring Shobhinaww Satyaa became a sleeper hit following strong word-of-mouth publicity. It reportedly collected more than Rs 150 crore worldwide within a month, bringing renewed attention to the saint's life and his birthplace, PTI reported.

World.title: India considers it a responsibility, not a favour, to provide aid to Sri Lanka as first responder: Rajnath to president Dissanayake
World.content:
Defence minister Rajnath Singh meets Sri Lankan president Anura Kumara Dissanayake

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Defence minister Rajnath conveyed greetings on behalf of PM Modi and underlined that the citizens of the two countries share deep friendship based on strong historical and civilisational links and people-to-people exchanges. He emphasised that as a closest friend and neighbour of Sri Lanka, âIndia considered it not a favour, but a responsibility to provide assistance as the first responder and would continue to do so in the future as wellâ.Sri Lankan president Dissanayake said his country would never allow its territory to be used for activities inimical to Indiaâs security interests. He also expressed his gratitude for the relief assistance provided by India as part of Op Sagar Bandhu during Cyclone Ditwah and the comprehensive rehabilitation package extended by New.Both leaders virtually inaugurated three Bailey bridges constructed by the Indian defence forces. The two sides also exchanged MoUs on upgradation of L70 guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force, and cooperation between NCC and National Defence Colleges of both the countries.Rajnath also met Sri Lankan PM Harini Amarasuriya. âWe exchanged views on a range of issues related to development cooperation, education and close cultural and civilisational ties,â he posted on X.He underlined that as âsister democracies with shared heritageâ, India and Sri Lanka should continue working towards a shared developmental vision for the peace and prosperity of the region. Rajnath also highlighted Sri Lanka's importance in India's Vision MAHASAGAR, saying the island nation holds a special place in the policy and would continue to do so in the future.Rajnath called for enhanced cooperation between India and Sri Lanka to shape a favourable and secure maritime environment and tackle emerging maritime challenges before they evolve into serious threats to developmental interests and brighter future. âSecure sea lanes, freedom of navigation, respect for international law and unhindered maritime trade are pivotal for collective security & prosperity of the Indian Ocean Region (IOR),â the defence minister said while addressing a gathering comprising Sri Lankan deputy minister of defence Aruna Jayasekara, commanders of the Sri Lankan three services.Rajnath said India and Sri Lanka are bound by the shared ocean, and maritime security is not a matter of abstract theory but a reality that shapes their trade, security and destinies. âBoth nations are central to any strategic discourse on maritime security in the region. Strong India-Sri Lanka maritime cooperation will be mutually beneficial and vital for collective growth and security,â he said.Referring to the challenges faced by our fishermen, the defence minister underscored that the issue needs to be addressed together. He observed that maritime cooperation should extend beyond the security framework to also cover areas like aquaculture, marine biotechnology, ocean science, protection and preservation of maritime environment and maritime tourism.He also suggested that the two countries can explore the establishment of a joint Maritime Humanitarian Assistance & Disaster Relief (HADR) system involving relevant agencies for a coordinated and rapid response to natural calamities and man-made disasters.Rajnath also laid a wreath at the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) Memorial in Battaramulla and paid homage to the bravehearts who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty.

World.title: India launches ORV Sagar Manthan, boosting ocean research fleet
World.content:
ORV Sagar Manthan, built under the Deep Ocean Mission at a cost of around Rs 840 crore, will boost Indiaâs ocean research capabilities.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Government on Wednesday launched state-of-the-art ocean research vessel ORV Sagar Manthan at Rishi Bankim Shipyard in Kolkata, boosting Indiaâs efforts towards self-reliance in oceanographic science and maritime technology.Constructed under Vertical-4 (Deep Ocean Survey and Exploration) of the governmentâs flagship Deep Ocean Mission (DOM) at a cost of around Rs 840 crore, the vessel is an all-weather, multidisciplinary platform. It is engineered to operate in extreme oceanic environments, including the Southern Ocean, with a projected service life of 30 years.The ORV Sagar Manthan, designed, engineered and constructed by defence public sector undertaking Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE), will gradually replace the iconic 43-year-old ORV Sagar Kanya, procured from Germany in 1983.âToday, the world knows very little about our oceans, yet they provide vital inputs about melting polar glaciers, maritime impact, and climate dynamics. Solid data collected by vessels like ORV Sagar Manthan will allow India to lead the global path in disaster prevention, take corrective environmental measures, and play a pivotal role in global ocean geopolitics,â said Union minister of earth sciences Jitendra Singh, who virtually joined the launch event.ORV Sagar Manthan will support multidisciplinary exploration along Indian Ocean mid-oceanic ridges to identify multi-metal hydrothermal sulphide mineralisation, establish environmental baselines and collect upper-air data. It integrates dynamic positioning, multibeam bathymetry, multichannel seismic systems, sub-bottom profiling, weather radar, drop keels and deployment facilities for remotely operated and autonomous underwater vehicles.

World.title: ‘Wanted to teach him a lesson’: Accused on assault that killed Manipuri musician
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The men accused of killing Manipuri musician Chongtham Vikram Singh in southeast Delhi allegedly wanted to âteach him a lessonâ for objecting to noise outside his home, but did not expect the assault to turn fatal, police said on Wednesday.

During questioning, the accused allegedly told police that they assaulted the 54-year-old musician with fists and blows after he objected to the commotion outside his residence in Kilokari, according to the police, as cited by news agency PTI.

Singh had on some occasions complained to the owner of a nearby dhaba about the noise caused by people gathering there, a senior police officer said. However, police had not received any formal complaint from Singh regarding the noise.

The dhaba remained open until around midnight and attracted customers from neighbouring areas as well as students living nearby, police said.

Police examine racial angle, dhaba ownerâs role

Police said they were examining all aspects of the case, including whether there was any racial angle. So far, the investigation has not revealed any instance of a racial slur being used against Singh during the altercation, a police source said.

The FIR registered at Sunlight Colony police station on the complaint of Singh's son mentions Section 103(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, pertaining to group murder in circumstances covered by the provision.





Police are awaiting the post-mortem report to ascertain the exact nature of the injuries sustained by Singh. Prima facie, he appears to have suffered internal injuries that led to his death.

The police are also examining the role of the dhaba owner and its operations. So far, no irregularity in the functioning of the establishment has come to light, sources said. Action would be taken against the owner if anything emerges during the investigation.

CCTV footage is being scrutinised and witnesses are being questioned to establish the sequence of events and the circumstances that led to the assault.

Singh died hours after assault

The incident took place around 11.30 pm on Sunday when Singh went downstairs after hearing a commotion outside his home.

According to the complaint, when his son heard his father shouting, he opened the door and saw a group of men kicking and punching him.

Singh subsequently returned upstairs but complained of breathlessness.

His 20-year-old son Yaiphaba took him to Holy Family Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries around 6 am the following day, police said.

Seven men have been arrested and a juvenile apprehended in connection with the case. The accused have been identified as Bharat Kumar, 19, Pramod, 26, Ramzan Khan, 22, Deepanshu, 21, Mohan Vishwakarma, 32, Vijay, 36, and Mannu, 26.

Northeast body seeks swift, impartial probe

The killing has sparked concern among members of Delhi's northeastern community, with several residents alleging that people from the region face racial slurs and discrimination in the national capital.

The North Eastern Students' Organisation (NESO) on Wednesday condemned Singh's killing and demanded a swift and impartial probe.

NESO chairman Samuel B Jyrwa said the incident was deeply disturbing and called for all those responsible to be brought to justice.

âIt is deeply disturbing that a person can lose his life merely for raising an objection to disturbance outside his own home. We demand a transparent and impartial investigation and exemplary punishment for every person found responsible,â Jyrwa said in a statement, as cited by PTI.

Jyrwa said the killing could not be viewed in isolation from what he described as continuing harassment, racial discrimination, stereotyping, intimidation and violence faced by people from the Northeast in different parts of mainland India.

âFor years, Northeastern citizens living, studying and working outside the region have repeatedly reported being subjected to racial slurs, verbal abuse, physical attacks, social discrimination and other forms of humiliation because of their appearance, identity and place of origin,â he alleged.

NESO urged authorities to treat the matter with seriousness and urgency and ensure that nobody responsible for the crime evades accountability.

âThe law must be applied firmly and equally, irrespective of the identity or background of the perpetrators,â Jyrwa said.

The organisation also called for stronger preventive measures, effective enforcement of the law, sensitisation of police and public institutions, and mechanisms to ensure the safety and dignity of people from the Northeast.

âThe loss of Chongtham Vikram Singh is not merely a personal tragedy for his family and loved ones, but a matter of deep concern for the entire Northeastern community,â Jyrwa said.

Who was Chongtham Vikram Singh?

Singh had lived in Kilokari for more than two decades. He was a well-known musician and guitarist, and had been the lead guitarist of the Manipur rock band Phoenix in the early 1980s.

He later worked as a music teacher and performer in Delhi.

NESO expressed solidarity with Singh's family and the people of Manipur and demanded justice for him and accountability for everyone found responsible for his death.

World.title: Brics summit in Delhi on September 12-13: Agenda, schedule and other details
World.content:
The two-day BRICS summit in New Delhi, set to kick-off Saturday, will focus on strengthening cooperation in food and energy security, health, disaster resilience and critical supply chains, as member countries seek to build greater resilience amid a fragmented geopolitical environment.

The summit, hosted by India under its 2026 chairship, will also cover trade, investment, connectivity and technology, while leaders are expected to exchange views on major global and regional developments.

Agenda

Building resilience

Under India's resilience pillar, leaders will discuss cooperation in areas including health, agriculture, food and energy security, disaster-risk reduction and critical supply chains.

The discussions come against the backdrop of disruptions caused by geopolitical conflicts and growing concerns over the resilience of global supply networks.

Trade, investment and technology

Strengthening intra-BRICS trade and investment, improving connectivity and expanding cooperation in high technology will also be among the key economic priorities. India has placed these areas at the centre of its broader effort to deepen cooperation among emerging economies.





Global governance

The summit will also focus on strengthening multilateralism and making global governance more inclusive. The first closed-door session on Saturday is titled âInclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism.â

Global and regional issues

Leaders will exchange views on global and regional developments and discuss areas of mutual interest, according to the Ministry of External Affairs.

Sunday's main session

The main open session on Sunday is titled âResilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth.â The summit will culminate with the release of the New Delhi Declaration.

BRICS summit schedule

Saturday (September 12)

2:35 pm: Closed-door session for BRICS member countries on âInclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralismâ.

4:25 pm: Leaders will tour the Bharat Innovates Exhibition.

5:05 pm: Leaders will assemble at Bharat Mandapam for the family photo, followed by a joint tree-planting ceremony.

7:30 pm: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will host a gala dinner for the leaders.

Sunday (September 13)

9:55 am: Leaders from BRICS member countries, partner nations and outreach invitees will begin arriving.

10:35 am: Official group photo.

10:50 am: Open session on âResilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growthâ.

The summit will conclude with the release of the New Delhi Declaration.

Who is attending?

Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Russian President Vladimir Putin, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto are among the leaders expected to attend the summit, reported PTI.

The summit comes against the backdrop of the global economy facing disruptions from the Russia-Ukraine war, the West Asia crisis, including concerns over the Strait of Hormuz, and the trade and tariff policies of the Trump administration.

With the grouping operating on consensus, questions also remain over whether members will agree on a joint statement, particularly amid differences between Iran and the UAE over the West Asia crisis.

BRICS originally comprised Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. The group expanded in 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia, while Indonesia joined in 2025.

Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam became BRICS partner countries in 2025.

The grouping now has 11 member countries, representing around 49.5% of the world's population, 40% of global GDP and 26% of global trade, according to the Indian government.

India assumed its fourth BRICS chairship on January 1 this year having previously chaired the grouping in 2012, 2016 and 2021.

India's chairship is guided by the theme âBuilding for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainabilityâ, with a stated focus on a people-centric approach rooted in the principle of âhumanity firstâ.

Under India's chairship, more than 350 meetings and high-level engagements have been held across more than 25 cities, covering the grouping's three broad pillars: political and security cooperation, economic and financial cooperation, and cultural and people-to-people exchanges.

World.title: Centre clears separate engineering cadre for Delhi PWD
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre has approved the Delhi government's proposal to create a separate engineering cadre for the Public Works Department (PWD), a move expected to give the capital greater control over its engineering workforce and help speed up infrastructure projects.

Under the decision, 3,214 sanctioned engineering posts across 36 categories in Delhi PWD will be separated from the

(CPWD) cadre and brought under an independent Delhi PWD Engineering Cadre.

Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta welcomed the approval, describing it as a historic step towards making Delhi a developed, safe and world-class capital.

The Delhi government said the separate cadre is intended to address a long-standing administrative issue and make the PWD's engineering system more responsive to the capital's specific requirements.

The proposal had earlier been approved by the Delhi Cabinet under Gupta's leadership.

The issue has remained pending for nearly 30 years. Until now, Delhi PWD's engineering services were largely dependent on the CPWD cadre, with appointments to its sanctioned posts being made through the Central government's system.

According to the Delhi government, this arrangement could sometimes make it difficult to take decisions quickly in line with Delhi's own development and administrative requirements.





Gupta said Delhi's infrastructure needs are distinct because of the scale and pace of development in the national capital. The city requires continuous construction and maintenance of roads, bridges, government buildings, offices and other public infrastructure.

With the creation of a separate cadre, the Delhi government will have greater control over its engineering workforce. It will be able to manage issues such as filling vacancies, ensuring the availability of engineers, monitoring projects and deploying officials according to the requirements of different works.

The government also expects the new arrangement to help build an engineering workforce more familiar with Delhi's local infrastructure challenges and development priorities.

The move comes as the government prepares to undertake several major construction and development projects. These include a new secretariat and mini-secretariats in all 11 districts, besides work related to mandis, sports grounds and other public facilities.

Roads, bridges and other infrastructure projects will also require sustained engineering support across the capital.

The government said the reform is not limited to changing the administrative structure of engineering posts. It is also intended to improve accountability and transparency in the execution of public works.

Gupta said that under the earlier system, instances involving deficiencies or irregularities in construction projects could sometimes make it difficult to fix responsibility, particularly when the concerned officer was transferred.

A separate Delhi PWD cadre, the government said, would allow the responsibilities of engineering officials and the monitoring of their work to be linked more closely with the Delhi government's administrative system.

The Centre's approval now provides the formal basis for Delhi PWD to establish an independent engineering cadre. The government believes the move will make the department more self-reliant and help ensure greater continuity in the planning, execution and supervision of infrastructure projects.

World.title: National Conference, Congress exchange barbs after Omar, Farooq stand for full version of Vande Mataram
World.content:
The Ruling National Conference (NC) and its ally the Congress traded barbs on Wednesday over the NC leadership’s decision to stand for all stanzas of the national song, Vande Mataram, after it was played at the inauguration of the International Film Festival Jammu & Kashmir (IFFJK) in Srinagar on September 7.

J&K Congress chief Tariq Hameed Karra, in a post on X, questioned Chief Minister Omar Abdullah and NC president Dr. Farooq Abdullah’s decision to stand for all stanzas of the song.

“National symbols, songs and traditions occupy a special place in the heart of every Indian. Their true strength lies in their ability to bind together a nation as diverse as ours. It is therefore a matter of concern that our alliance partners chose to sing the full version of Vande Mataram, disregarding the considered evolution of the song’s place in India’s national life, not merely during the freedom movement, but through the constitutional journey of the Republic thereafter. The adopted version represented a conscious balance preserving the historic ... ,” said Mr. Karra.

Mr. Karra’s post followed a social media statement by Congress General Secretary K. C. Venugopal, who posted the video of the Srinagar ceremony in which NC leaders stood for all the stanzas.

“The full version of Vande Mataram sits uneasily with the syncretic and pluralist ethos that our freedom fighters envisioned and nurtured for India. For us, the considered judgment of Mahatma Gandhi, Pandit Nehru, Sardar Patel, Subhash Chandra Bose, Rajendra Prasad, Acharya Narendra Dev, Maulana Azad, Sarojini Naidu and J.B. Kripalani — shaped in no small part by the counsel of Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore — remains paramount,” said Mr. Venugopal.

Honour freedom fighters

In the post, the Congress leader said, “With respect and humility, we would like our allies to honour the wisdom and judgment of our freedom fighters and stand with us in singing only the version of this beautiful and historic song that they adopted. That version was chosen deliberately, to keep the song from being communalised — a threat as real today as it was then. Upholding it is how we uphold the secular, inclusive character of our Republic.”

The Congress posts on social media platforms drew a sharp reaction from NC leaders. NC legislator Tanvir Sadiq shared videos of swearing-in ceremonies involving a Congress chief minister and asked Mr. Karra to comment.

NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar said, “The NC’s official position is that it is not a votary of either the first two stanzas or six stanzas of the national song. However, it is a Constitutional obligation, and every holder of a Constitutional office has to accept it, whether it is the CM, a MP or anyone else.”

Referring to videos from the Congress-ruled states of Karnataka and Telangana, Mr. Dar said, “The chief ministers stand for all the six stanzas. However, we do not want to make this a controversy. We are not here to fight the Congress.”

Meanwhile, the Opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) also criticised the NC. “On every key issue, Rahul Gandhi took a stand, his J&K ally NC caved and rolled out the red carpet for the BJP. No condemnation on the Waqf amendment Bill. No condemnation of SIR fraud. Justifying EVM rigging concerns. Accepted Vande Mataram’s addition. INDIA bloc in elections, BJP’s silent enabler in practice,” said PDP leader and legislator Waheed-ur-Rehman Parra.

World.title: After a two-year delay, Chennai airport’s plaza to be opened on Saturday
World.content:
Air passengers can finally heave a sigh of relief as Minister of Civil Aviation Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu will inaugurate the plaza housing the second cab pick-up point at Chennai airport on September 12.

This means, air passengers who book cabs, can board from opposite the T1 Domestic Terminal, instead of having to travel to the multilevel car parking. It is to be noted that the cab pick-up point at the west wing of the multilevel car parking too will continue as usual.

With the intention of providing a relaxing area for arriving passengers and visitors, Airports Authority of India (AAI) designed a plaza opposite to the T1 Domestic Terminal. The construction work on the plaza commenced in 2023 and was to be completed in October 2024.

In the meantime, the AAI moved the cab pick-up point from opposite to the T1 Domestic Terminal to the second floor of the west wing of multilevel car parking facility, and this did not go well with air passengers who vehemently opposed the move. After a year’s delay in construction, the opening of the plaza was deferred for the past nine months owing to various reasons.

Officials of AAI said they have completed a dry run before opening the plaza. “Passengers who make bookings through cab aggregators such as Ola, Uber, Rapido, Fast Track, Red Taxi, and Prepaid Taxi will be able to board the cab from the plaza. These cabs, which wait inside the multilevel car parking, can enter the plaza only if they have confirmed bookings,” an official said.

“But, passengers who have to take the other private yellow board vehicles (like companies that send cars for their employees or clients) will continue to board from the west wing of the parking lot only,” the official added.

“This is because all the vehicles cannot head to the plaza and it may cause congestion,” another official said.

“Also, boarding taxis from the plaza will be most convenient for those arriving at the T1 Domestic Terminal. The rest of them arriving at T2 or T4 may find it more convenient to head to the parking area. But even if they want to come only to plaza to take a taxi, buggy vehicles will be present to drop them off,” he added.

World.title: Free online coaching scheme for competitive exams to be launched on September 10
World.content:
The State government has decided to provide free online coaching for various competitive examinations to eligible candidates under the ‘Mukhyamanthri Vidyarthi Sahaya Hasta’ scheme, and the Higher Education Department will launch the scheme on Thursday (September 10, 2026).

Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, Higher Education Minister Basavaraj Rayaraddi said, “The main objective of the scheme is to equip students to face competitive examinations with confidence and without stress. Children of farmers and those from rural areas should not be deprived of opportunities to appear for competitive examinations. The Higher Education Department is implementing this scheme free of cost with the aim of helping them secure government jobs.”

“The scheme is being implemented at a total cost of ₹9 crore for around 90,000 candidates, and each candidate will be provided three months of free online coaching through a selected coaching institute,” he added.

Free online coaching will be provided for various competitive examinations, including SDA, FDA, PDO, PSI and Gazetted Probationers (GP). Eligible candidates can receive coaching for a maximum of three examinations.

The training will include an online Learning Management System (LMS), study material, online classes and a doubt-clearing facility. Recorded classes, session-wise multiple-choice questions, mock tests, previous years’ question papers and question banks will also be provided.

Eligible candidates can apply online through the Seva Sindhu website and Grama One centres. Candidates will receive a unique ID upon registration and can access the portal using a one-time password sent to their mobile phones. The system will also track attendance, participation, test performance and progress. A consolidated report has to be submitted to the department every 15 days.

The coaching will cover general studies subjects such as history, geography, Indian economy and polity, science and environment, logical reasoning, data interpretation, current affairs, Kannada and English language skills, and digital literacy. Exam-specific subjects and communication papers will also be covered. General studies will be common to all competitive examination preparations.

7.5% reservation for rural children

Mr. Rayaraddi also announced that the State government has decided to provide 7.5% reservation in higher education for students who studied in government schools and colleges in rural areas from Class 1 to 12.

“Already, 15% reservation has been provided for students from rural areas in higher education, including admission to professional courses. However, students who studied in private educational institutions are also availing themselves of this benefit. As a result, poor students studying in government schools and colleges in rural areas are being deprived of opportunities. Realising this, the State government has taken steps to bifurcate this reservation and provide 7.5% reservation to candidates who studied in government schools and colleges in rural areas,” he added.

He further said that the reservation would provide greater opportunities for students to study in good medical and engineering colleges, and that children of farmers and those from middle- and lower-middle-class families in rural areas would benefit.

World.title: ‘Rahman wants to visit India, but agenda has to be set first’
World.content:
Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is keen to visit India at the earliest but is concerned about take away points and achievements that he will have to produce before his audience back home after a visit of this nature, said a diplomatic source of Bangladesh to The Hindu on Wednesday (September 9, 2026)

The official said that Prime Minister Rahman might have skipped the multilateral BRICS summit for which he was invited by India, but that does not mean that he is trying to avoid an immediate and important neighbour like India which has contributed and sacrificed immensely during Bangladesh’s Liberation War of 1971. PM Rahman is aware that he may have to visit Delhi in a bilateral framework by November or early December, as the Ganga Water Treaty needs to be renewed at the earliest as it will otherwise lapse by the end of December, said the official.

Also Read | The trust deficit in India-Bangladesh ties

The official said that Mr. Rahman’s visit requires setting of the agenda through intensive meetings between the officials of the two sides that are yet to begin. But Dhaka believes that apart from the Ganga Water Treaty which is a “rolling achievement” as it is expected to be renewed after having survived for 30 years, there is a need to look at other areas where the bilateral relationship is stuck.

“For example, in case of restarting full scale visa facilities, lifting of trade restrictions that were imposed during the interim government in Dhaka, and usage of land ports, and restarting of full scale commercial relationship are some of the areas where there is possibility of setting up some solid goals for achievement,” said the official.

He also pointed out that one area where India could send a positive message is in the field of energy as Bangladesh is suffering from an acute crunch in energy supply. “It will be a confidence building measure if India can assist Bangladesh in dealing with this challenge,” said the official who indicated that Bangladesh is looking at commercial and consular issues separately from hard political issues like Sheikh Hasina’s presence in India.

The official described the Ganga Water Treaty as a success of bilateral diplomacy that was sealed in 1996 during Sheikh Hasina’s first prime ministerial stint, and subsequently functioned in BNP years in 2001-’06. “Failing to renew this treaty before the year end will reflect negatively on the relationship,” said the official noting that delaying this renewal is counterproductive as already there are voices in India like that of JD(U) MP Sanjay Jha who have started opposing renewal of the treaty citing that the treaty does not benefit Bihar. “Prolonging this process will encourage such critics of this treaty to come forward,” he said.

A visit by PM Rahman, he said, has to be designed in such a way that it will kick start the India-Bangladesh relationship to its fullest potential. “Only then Prime Minister can return home with a substantial achievement in hand from Delhi,” said the official who added that PM Rahman is personally committed to holding dialogue with India at the highest level.

The official noted that India’s High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi has been holding rounds of discussions in Dhaka with multiple high-level officials including with the newly elected President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir but the bureaucrats-level talks are necessary to create an agenda for PM Rahman’s visit. “We are open minded about building an agenda for a visit by our Prime Minister. On some issues there can be relaxation of our positions and on certain issues we would prefer the relation to move ahead,” he said.

Also Read | Sheikh Hasina’s media event can hurt ties with India: Bangladesh

The Hindu was told that Bangladesh expects India to be mindful of the fact that Sheikh Hasina’s accusations against Tarique Rahman are not rational as Mr. Rahman is an elected leader. “However, we are satisfied by the fact that a fresh press event featuring members of Sheikh Hasina’s party and her supporters was prevented by India. That is a constructive message from India and we have taken note of it,” said the official.

In this connection, he said that BNP leaders remember that in 2018, India denied entry to Lord Alexander Carlile, legal adviser to Bangladesh Nationalist Party’s then Chairperson Khaleda Zia. Lord Carlile was expected to address a press conference against Sheikh Hasina , who was Prime Minister of Bangladesh at that time.

Prime Minister Rahman was invited to attend the BRICS summit in Delhi as the head of BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) between September 12-13 and bureaucrats-level consultation was ongoing between the two sides over the visit when deposed PM Sheikh Hasina addressed a press conference at the Foreign Correspondents Club here on August 5. Bangladesh’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs in response accused Hasina of committing violent crimes and expressed “outrage” over the event.

World.title: GVMC chief calls for green Ganesh celebrations
World.content:
Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) Commissioner Ketan Garg has urged citizens to install Ganesh idols made of natural clay and avoid those made of Plaster of Paris (PoP), chemical colours and other materials that can harmf the environment.

In a release on Tuesday, Mr Garg advised pandal organisers to avoid single-use plastic and other banned plastic items for pandal decorations, and instead choose eco-friendly alternatives. He said: ”Organisers should set up Ganesh pandals only after obtaining the necessary permissions from the concerned departments.” They should ensure cleanliness in and around pandals every day and segregate wet and dry waste before handing it over to the GVMC sanitation personnel.

Flowers, puja materials, food waste and other waste should not be dumped on roads, in drains or at public places, he said
